title: PROSPECTS FOR THE APPLICATION OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN THE ACCOUNTING AND AUDITING SYSTEM
summary: Purpose of the research – The purpose of this study is to examine the application areas of modern digital technologies in the accounting and auditing system, evaluate their impact on financial reporting, audit quality, and managerial efficiency, identify the existing challenges, and develop scientifically grounded recommendations regarding future development prospects. Research methodology – The study is based on a systematic approach and employs comparative analysis, content analysis, induction, and deduction methods. Contemporary scientific literature, international accounting and auditing standards, and studies on digital technologies were analyzed. Practical implications of the research – The findings of this study provide practical guidance for the digital transformation of accounting and auditing systems, the automation of audit procedures, the improvement of financial reporting quality, and the enhancement of managerial decision-making processes within organizations. Research findings – The study demonstrates that artificial intelligence, blockchain, Big Data, cloud computing, and robotic process automation (RPA) significantly improve the efficiency of accounting and auditing systems. Originality and scientific novelty – The study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the application of digital technologies in accounting and auditing by systematically analyzing the influence of various digital solutions on financial management 2 and audit quality. It presents scientifically grounded conclusions regarding the benefits, challenges, and future prospects of digital transformation and offers practical recommendations for the effective implementation of innovative technologies in accounting and auditing systems.

title: Green finance policy and environmental decoupling: evidence from China
summary: As a policy instrument designed to promote coordinated economic growth and environmental protection in China, the Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones (GFP) may play an important role in fostering environmental decoupling, yet their effectiveness remains unclear. This article provides new evidence on the effectiveness of China’s green finance policy by examining its effects on carbon decoupling and haze decoupling. Using balanced panel data of Chinese cities from 2012 to 2021, we employ a difference-in-differences (DID) model and find that GFP promotes carbon decoupling but has no significant effect on haze decoupling. Mechanism analysis reveals that green innovation, green bond development, and environmental regulation are important channels through which GFP promotes carbon decoupling. Further analyses show that the carbon decoupling effect is more pronounced in regions with higher levels of financial technology (Fintech) development and greater public environmental concern. Moreover, GFP also generates special spatial spillover effects, promoting carbon decoupling in neighbouring areas. These findings have important policy implications for enhancing the environmental effectiveness of China’s green finance policy.

title: Role of Corporate Governance in Business Success
summary: Corporate governance has emerged as an essential component of modern business management and sustainable corporate development. It provides a framework through which companies are directed, controlled and held accountable to shareholders and other stakeholders. Effective corporate governance promotes transparency, accountability, ethical decision-making, responsible management and protection of stakeholder interests. In India, the legal framework governing corporate governance has developed significantly through the Companies Act, 2013, the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. These legal mechanisms seek to strengthen the functioning of boards, independent directors, audit committees, disclosure systems and shareholder protection. This paper examines the relationship between corporate governance and business success from a legal and analytical perspective. It argues that corporate governance should not be regarded merely as a compliance requirement but as a strategic mechanism capable of improving investor confidence, reducing corporate risks, preventing fraud, enhancing reputation and promoting long-term business sustainability. The paper further analyses major corporate failures in India to demonstrate the consequences of weak governance and examines the role of transparency, independent oversight and accountability in creating sustainable enterprises. It concludes that effective corporate governance creates value not only for shareholders but also for employees, creditors, consumers and society.

title: The Evolution of Corporate Governance: A Comparative Study of the Cadbury Committee Report (1992), Sarbanes-Oxley Act (2002), and the Indian Corporate Governance Framework
summary: Corporate governance has emerged as a critical mechanism for ensuring accountability, transparency, and sustainable value creation in modern corporations, particularly in the wake of high-profile corporate failures that exposed weaknesses in board oversight, financial reporting, and internal controls. This study undertakes a comparative analysis of three landmark frameworks: the Cadbury Report (1992) of the United Kingdom, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (2002) of the United States, and the contemporary Indian corporate governance regime anchored in the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI regulations. The purpose is to examine the evolution of core governance principles, especially board independence, the role and composition of audit committees, and mechanisms of corporate accountability, across different institutional and regulatory contexts. Major findings indicate that while the Cadbury Report laid foundational voluntary principles centred on board structure and financial integrity, Sarbanes-Oxley introduced rigorous, mandatory internal-control and certification requirements, and the Indian framework has synthesised both approaches into a hybrid model that balances statutory mandates with market-oriented disclosure norms. The study concludes that corporate governance has evolved from principle-based, comply-or-explain systems toward more prescriptive, enforcement-oriented regimes, yet retains a common emphasis on independent oversight and accountability as universal safeguards against managerial opportunism.

title: Lean Supply Chain 4.0: An Integrative Literature Review of Digital Technologies, Supply Chain Coordination, and Operational Performance
summary: Abstract - With increasingly complex production systems there is an increased need for efficient, flexible, coordinated and sustainable supply chains. Lean manufacturing techniques and Lean Six Sigma (LSS) have been developed to reduce waste, variability and improve quality. Industry 4.0 techniques such as IoT, AI, Big Data, Digital Twins, Blockchain and Cyber Physical Systems provide new opportunities to monitor, predict, automate and share information using digital technologies. Despite having similar aims in improving processes, there are challenges to combine Lean techniques with Industry 4.0 techniques within supply chain networks due to differences in technology, organisational barriers, lack of skills and a lack of a framework that can be applied universally. This paper provides an integrative literature review that focuses on literature related to SCM, Lean and Lean Six Sigma, Industry 4.0, digital transformation and supply chain coordination. The literature has been split into themes so that key findings can be identified. Relationships between research areas have also been identified along with gaps in the literature. The synthesis shows that digital technologies can be used to improve Lean within processes. However, digital technologies do not automatically improve supply chain performance. It depends on how well digital technologies are aligned with process maturity, organisational preparedness, information sharing and continual improvement. A key gap in the research was found to be the absence of an integrated framework that can explain how digital technologies and Lean/Lean Six Sigma can be combined with supply chain coordination to improve operational performance, resilience and sustainability. A conceptual research framework has been proposed along with suggestions for future empirical and modelling research.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE QUALITY AND EXTERNAL AUDIT QUALITY ON EARNINGS MANAGEMENT IN NIGERIA’S OIL AND GAS SECTOR: A POST-COVID-19 PERIOD
summary: This study investigates the impact of corporate governance quality and external audit quality on earnings management in Nigeria‘s oil and gas sector during the post-COVID- 19 period. Drawing from 56 firm-year observations of seven listed companies between the periods 2018-2025, the study explores both discretionary accruals and real earnings management (REM) as key proxies for earnings manipulation. Using ordinary least square panel regression models, the findings reveal a significant increase in earnings management practices following the COVID-19 pandemic, indicating heightened managerial incentives to manage earnings under economic pressure. It recommends stronger regulatory oversight, enhanced board structures, and improved audit practices to safeguard financial reporting integrity. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers, regulators, and stakeholders seeking to strengthen institutional responses to future economic shocks. title: Corporate governance and green innovation performance: a TCCM-based systematic literature review
summary: This study reviews and synthesizes literature linking corporate governance mechanisms to green innovation performance. It examines how board structure, ownership patterns, executive incentives, and ESG practices shape firms' pursuit of sustainability-driven innovation across institutional contexts. Using the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis) protocol and TCCM (Theory-Context-Characteristics-Methodology) framework, the review analyses 213 articles published between 2015 and 2025. Bibliometric mapping and content analysis identify foundations, methodological trends, and differences in the governance-innovation nexus. Findings show that board diversity, independence, and environmental competence improve green innovation performance by supporting perspectives and stakeholder responsiveness. Ownership structure, CEO duality, and ESG disclosure influence innovation outcomes, with effects varying by institutional quality and industry context. Quantitative and single-theory approaches dominate, highlighting the need for integrated frameworks and methods. The study positions governance as both a compliance mechanism and a driver of competitiveness and value creation, providing a synthesis and a research agenda for sustainability-focused corporate governance.

title: How data asset accounting enhances inclusive finance: an evolutionary analysis using signaling game models
summary: Information asymmetry remains a major obstacle to inclusive finance for micro and small enterprises (MSEs). This study develops an evolutionary signaling game model in which boundedly rational MSEs and banks adapt their strategies through repeated interactions to examine whether observable data asset disclosures can serve as a supplementary financing signal under emerging accounting systems. The results show that when banks consider observable data asset disclosures in lending decisions and set loan amounts within an appropriate range, high-potential MSEs are more likely to continue digital transformation and disclose capitalized data assets, allowing banks to improve their assessment of firm quality and achieve a separating equilibrium. However, excessively high or low loan amounts weaken the signaling mechanism. The study suggests that observable data asset disclosures may help reduce financing-related information asymmetry under appropriate institutional conditions. While the model is calibrated to China’s emerging data asset accounting framework, the proposed mechanism may also provide theoretical insights for other economies undergoing digital accounting reforms.

title: Reflections on the Application of FinTech in ESG Risk Management under the Background of Sustainable Finance
summary: As China's green financial system continues to improve and sustainable finance steadily expands, it has effectively promoted the green and low-carbon transformation and upgrading of the domestic capital market. Against the backdrop of the routine development of green investment and financing activities, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risk management has become a core tool for financial institutions to ensure compliance and control green credit risks, directly determining the quality of risk management across various green financial services. Traditional ESG assessment systems primarily rely on static corporate disclosures and manual expertise for risk evaluation, resulting in a relatively coarse overall approach that struggles to adapt to the new industry landscape following the full implementation of low-carbon policies. These systems commonly suffer from inherent shortcomings such as delayed data updates, strong subjectivity in human judgment, reactive risk mitigation, and insufficient coverage of risk dimensions, making them inadequate to meet today’s demand for refined, high-quality green finance development. Leveraging cutting-edge fintech technologies—including big data, blockchain, and artificial intelligence—financial institutions can achieve quantitative risk assessment, dynamic monitoring, and end-to-end closed-loop management of ESG risks, significantly enhancing the intelligence and precision of green risk governance. However, in practice, multiple real-world barriers still hinder the effective application of fintech in ESG risk management. Issues such as significant disparities in data quality, structural biases in algorithms, lack of standardization in industry-wide ESG evaluation frameworks, and lagging regulatory evolution substantially diminish the enabling power of digital technologies. Based on current industry practices, this paper systematically identifies key application scenarios of fintech in ESG risk management, deeply analyzes critical implementation bottlenecks, and proposes targeted optimization pathways to provide practical guidance for Chinese financial institutions in building standardized, digitalized ESG risk control systems.

title: Akses Green Finance bagi UMKM di Indonesia: Hambatan Struktural, Kesesuaian Instrumen, dan Strategi Penguatan melalui Narrative Literature Review
summary: Aims: This study aims to analyze access to green finance among micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia by identifying structural barriers, enabling factors, and the suitability of green financing instruments for MSMEs’ characteristics and stages of green practice adoption. It also develops a conceptual framework to explain the interaction between MSMEs’ internal readiness, financial institutions’ assessment mechanisms, and policy ecosystem support in expanding access to green finance. Method: This study employs a narrative literature review approach. Relevant literature was retrieved through Google Scholar and GARUDA, while publication metadata were cross-checked through Crossref. A critical thematic analysis was conducted on relevant scholarly articles, regulations, and institutional reports to identify recurring barriers, evaluate the suitability of financing instruments, and synthesize strategies for strengthening MSMEs’ access to green finance in Indonesia. Results: The findings indicate that barriers to green finance access emerge from the interaction of three dimensions. First, the internal MSME dimension includes limited financial and environmental literacy, inadequate financial record-keeping, administrative constraints, and limited capacity to bear the upfront costs of green investment. Second, the financial institution dimension involves collateral requirements, risk assessment practices, transaction costs, and the limited availability of financing instruments suited to MSMEs’ scale of operations. Third, the policy ecosystem dimension encompasses the clarity of green business criteria, credit guarantee support, business assistance, and digital infrastructure. The review also finds that evidence concerning digital literacy and fintech utilization primarily explains the adoption of green practices rather than direct access to financing. Therefore, financing access, green practice adoption, and business performance should be treated as distinct outcomes. Novelty: The novelty of this study lies in developing a three-layer conceptual framework that integrates MSMEs’ readiness, financial institutions’ assessment mechanisms, and policy ecosystem support, while distinguishing financing access from green practice adoption and business performance. The framework emphasizes the importance of aligning financing instruments with MSMEs’ characteristics and stages of green adoption. In practical terms, proportionate financing requirements, credit guarantees, financial and environmental assistance, and evaluation indicators covering applications, approvals, rejections, access costs, and environmental benefits should be developed. The proposed framework remains conceptual and therefore requires empirical testing using actual financing data.

title: Smart strategies for a sustainable future: Bridging green finance, smart technologies, and sustainable energy efficiency to combat environmental degradation
summary: Rising environmental degradation (ED) is a global phenomenon. While various environmental initiatives have been introduced across disciplines, mitigating environmental degradation remains a critical challenge. Recently, the world has emphasized the importance of smart technologies, green finance, and stringent government policies as additional tools for environmental sustainability; therefore, it is essential to clarify the empirical evidence on their effectiveness for environmental policymakers. This study evaluates income, population in large cities, smart technologies, green finance, sustainable energy efficiency, and government policy as environmental determinants for nine OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) nations from 2012 to 2023. Using panel quantile regression and fully modified ordinary least squares, the empirical findings reveal that the population of large cities and sustainable energy efficiency are positively associated with ED. Conversely, income shows an inverse connection and contributes to sustainability. In the context of smart technologies, this study focuses on digital transformation (DT) and artificial intelligence and finds a significant role for DT in environmental management. This study employs two proxies for green finance: green foreign direct investment and green bonds, both of which exhibit unusual behavior with respect to the intended theme. Finally, the moderating effect of green finance and smart technologies on sustainable energy efficiency doesn't support environmental management. This study also offers valuable suggestions for achieving long-term environmental sustainability.

title: Digital transformation of regions and territorial communities of Ukraine: problems and ways to solve them
summary: The article examines the challenges of digital transformation in Ukraine’s regions and territorial communities amid full-scale war and limited organizational and investment resources. The article identifies significant spatial digital divides between regions and territorial communities, as well as between regional centers and peripheral communities. Data from the Digital Transformation Index of the Regions of Ukraine for 2024–2025 reveal a polarization in digital development, and the “Digital Economy” sub-index is one of the index’s weakest components. The key problems of digitalization have been characterized, in particular: the destruction of digital infrastructure in frontline territories, residual financing of informatization in communities, communities’ low capacity to attract investment resources, a shortage of IT specialists, a deteriorating demographic situation, including changes in the age structure of the population of rural communities, and cybersecurity threats. The authors propose directions and tools to address these problems within Ukraine’s post-war recovery strategy. The authors argue that the digitalization of public administration and the digitalization of the economy are relatively autonomous processes that develop at different rates and with different effectiveness. The following directions for solving the identified problems have been proposed: state support for the development of digital infrastructure in mountainous and frontline territories, reducing the energy dependence of telecommunications, developing local digital education hubs, expanding the Trembita system and introducing standard digital solutions for communities, developing e-democracy tools, and supporting the digitalization of small and medium-sized enterprises through the Diia. Business network, regional IT clusters, and co-financing programs. Under wartime conditions, digitalization has proven to be a factor in regions’ security capacity and should be an integral part of Ukraine’s Recovery Plan and the strategy for integration into the EU Digital Single Market. Keywords: sustainable regional development, territorial community, local authorities, decentralization, cooperation, organizational and administrative mechanism, strategic planning, local budgets, digital technologies, public-private partnership, European integration.

title: Microsoft Excel As a Tool for Digitizing Financial Records and Supporting Decision-Making Among MSMEs in Dharmasraya Regency in The Era of Digital Transformation
summary: This study aims to understand the use of Microsoft Excel as a tool for digitalizing financial records and supporting decision-making among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Dharmasraya Regency. The study focuses on transaction-recording practices, the use of financial information for operational decisions, perceived benefits, challenges, and support needs. It is designed as a descriptive qualitative field study. Primary data are planned to be collected through semi-structured interviews with MSME owners or managers, observation of bookkeeping practices, and authorized documentation. Secondary data include government statistics, local planning documents, accounting standards, and scholarly articles on Excel-based financial reporting for MSMEs. Data analysis will involve data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Existing literature indicates that spreadsheets can support transaction recording and financial summaries; however, their practical value depends on complete data entry, user understanding, formula checking, and file security. title: Green Credit, Financing Constraints, And Corporate Green Transformation: A Financial Resource Allocation Perspective
summary: Green credit has become an important policy instrument for promoting sustainable development and integrating environmental considerations into financial resource allocation. As environmental concerns and climate-related risks increasingly influence economic activities, commercial banks are expected to play a greater role in supporting environmentally sustainable projects while maintaining financial stability. Where economic development and environmental sustainability are important policy priorities, green credit provides a potential mechanism for directing financial resources toward environmentally responsible industries. Drawing on financial intermediation theory and credit risk management perspectives, this study explores the channels through which green credit may influence commercial banks' credit risk. Green credit may reduce credit risk by encouraging banks to incorporate environmental factors into borrower assessments, strengthen lending standards, and identify potential risks associated with environmental regulations and unsustainable business practices. By directing financing toward environmentally responsible enterprises, banks may reduce their exposure to borrowers vulnerable to environmental and regulatory changes, thereby improving loan portfolio quality. These factors suggest that the relationship between green credit and credit risk may depend on banks' lending capabilities, borrower characteristics, and institutional conditions. The study is expected to contribute to the literature on sustainable finance by providing insights into the role of green credit in banking risk management within an emerging-market context. Its findings may also offer practical implications for commercial banks seeking to balance environmental responsibility with prudent lending decisions, as well as for policymakers developing green finance frameworks to support sustainable economic development and financial stability in Indonesia.

title: Advancing sustainable financing through pandemic bond: a Bayesian model averaging approach to liquidity premia
summary: Abstract Pandemic bonds, as a subtype of catastrophe (CAT) bonds, are designed to transfer public health risks to capital markets, yet they face substantial liquidity risk due to their nascent market structure and limited risk design. Using a relatively small sample from 2020 to 2024, we apply Bayesian model averaging (BMA) and interpretable machine learning (IML) to examine the associations of macroeconomic and bond-specific characteristics with liquidity premia across market phases. We find that the average liquidity premium of natural catastrophe bonds (1364 bps) is substantially higher than that of pandemic bonds (452 bps), potentially reflecting differences in bond characteristics and contractual structures. The estimates suggest that higher ESG scores and higher disclosed health scores are associated with lower estimated pandemic-bond premia, with health-score categories receiving slightly greater posterior inclusion support than ESG in the joint specification. Pandemic bond premia are higher during hard market phases, while several predictors receive greater posterior inclusion support during soft markets. Overall, the results suggest that incorporating a health-specific index, alongside insights from traditional CAT and green bond design, could enhance the resilience of pandemic bonds and strengthen their role in sustainable development.

title: OWNERSHIP STRUCTURE AND EARNINGS MANAGEMENT PRACTICES OF LISTED CONSUMER GOODS FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: This research investigated the influence of ownership structure on earnings management within publicly traded consumer goods companies in Nigeria. The study specifically examined the impact of director ownership, institutional ownership, and block ownership on earnings management. The research utilised an ex-post facto design and leveraged panel data from the annual reports of 16 selected enterprises out of a total of 21 consumer goods firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) for the period 2015– 2024. Earnings management was assessed by discretionary accruals derived from the Modified Jones Model (1995). Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, diagnostic assessments, and panel regression methodologies were utilised for data analysis. The results indicated that director ownership exerts a negative and significant influence on earnings management, suggesting that heightened director shareholding limits earnings manipulation. Institutional ownership exhibited a positive yet negligible impact on earnings management, indicating that institutional investors do not substantially affect earnings management methods inside the tested firms. Moreover, block ownership demonstrated a positive and significant influence on earnings management, suggesting that ownership concentration may promote earnings manipulation. The research determines that ownership structure markedly affects profits management techniques within publicly traded consumer goods companies in Nigeria. The study advocates for companies to promote appropriate levels of director ownership to align the interests of management and shareholders, while regulatory bodies should intensify oversight of firms with concentrated ownership structures to safeguard minority shareholders and improve the quality of financial reporting. Keywords: Ownership structure, director ownership, institutional ownership, block ownership, earnings management, consumer goods firms, Nigeria.

title: Corporate Governance and Financial Transparency in Indian Companies
summary: Corporate governance and financial transparency determine whether investors, lenders and the public can trust a company with their resources. This project examines how these two concepts have developed and operate in Indian companies, with particular emphasis on listed public companies. The study begins by explaining the concepts and the principal theories, namely agency, stewardship, stakeholder and principal-principal perspectives. It then traces the evolution of Indian governance norms from the voluntary code of the Confederation of Indian Industry and the work of the Birla, Naresh Chandra, Narayana Murthy, Irani and Kotak committees to the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015. The report analyses board structure, independent directors, committees, related party transactions, whistle-blowing, financial reporting under Ind AS, auditor independence and the role of the National Financial Reporting Authority. Five cases, namely Satyam, Tata Sons, IL&FS, the Infosys whistle-blower complaints and Think & Learn, are used to illustrate how failures arise and how regulation has responded. The study concludes that India's legal framework is now broadly comparable to that of leading economies, but that concentrated ownership, doubtful independence of directors, slow enforcement and formalistic compliance continue to limit its effectiveness. It recommends measures to strengthen independent directors, audit quality, enforcement, related party oversight and whistle-blower protection. Keywords: corporate governance, financial transparency, SEBI, Companies Act 2013, independent directors, audit, Ind AS, India.

title: Peran Corporate Governance dalam Meningkatkan Integritas Pelaporan Keuangan: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis atas Dewan Komisaris, Komite Audit, dan Audit Internal
summary: Abstract Objective: This study aims to examine the role of corporate governance in safeguarding financial reporting integrity, with particular emphasis on the board of commissioners, audit committee, and internal audit function. It seeks to identify the governance mechanisms most consistently associated with financial reporting quality and explain the factors underlying variations in empirical findings. Method: This study employs a limited systematic literature review guided by the PRISMA 2020 framework. A total of 39 records were identified through four search queries, of which 13 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the synthesis. The selected studies were analyzed using a narrative-thematic approach to identify recurring patterns, contextual differences, and inconsistencies in the relationships between corporate governance mechanisms and financial reporting integrity. Results: The synthesis reveals three main patterns. First, the audit committee demonstrates the most consistent association with financial reporting quality, particularly through its independence, expertise, size, and meeting frequency. Second, the effectiveness of independent commissioners is contingent on measurement approaches and regulatory contexts. In Indonesian studies, their effect is often statistically insignificant when their proportion merely meets the minimum regulatory threshold. Third, internal audit contributes more effectively to financial reporting oversight when professional competence and independence are present simultaneously, with its effectiveness further strengthened by the involvement of risk oversight committees. Differences in the proxies used to measure financial reporting integrity emerge as a major source of inconsistency across studies. Conclusion/Novelty/Implications: This study proposes a three-layer conceptual framework of financial reporting oversight integrating the board of commissioners, audit committee, and internal audit function. Its contribution lies in explaining how these mechanisms interact and why their effectiveness varies across institutional and measurement contexts. The findings highlight the need to strengthen substantive independence, professional expertise, and coordination among oversight mechanisms rather than relying solely on formal compliance with regulatory requirements. Future research should develop more consistent measures of financial reporting integrity and empirically test the proposed framework across different industries and regulatory settings.

title: SUSTENTABILIDADE E ESG EM PARQUES TEMÁTICOS: REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA E ANÁLISE DOCUMENTAL DE EXPERIÊNCIAS BRASILEIRAS E INTERNACIONAIS
summary: Este artigo analisa a incorporação da sustentabilidade e dos princípios ambientais, sociais e de governança (ESG) em parques temáticos, mediante revisão integrativa da literatura e análise documental de empreendimentos brasileiros e internacionais selecionados. A revisão reuniu 17 estudos científicos, complementados por documentos institucionais e corporativos. A análise considerou práticas ambientais, sociais e de governança, mecanismos de formalização, indicadores, transparência e integração estratégica da sustentabilidade. Nos empreendimentos internacionais selecionados, identificaram-se evidências documentais mais frequentes de formalização das práticas ESG, especialmente quanto à divulgação de metas, indicadores e mecanismos de governança. Nos casos brasileiros, foram observadas iniciativas heterogêneas, com diferentes níveis de detalhamento e disponibilidade de informações públicas. Essas diferenças devem ser interpretadas com cautela, uma vez que a documentação disponível não permite estabelecer uma classificação conclusiva do desempenho ou da maturidade ESG dos empreendimentos. O estudo contribui para a discussão sobre a aplicação do ESG ao turismo de entretenimento e identifica oportunidades para o desenvolvimento de indicadores específicos para parques temáticos.

title: U.S.-CHINA RIVALRY OVER CRITICAL MINERALS: STRATEGIC IMPLICATIONS FOR GEOPOLITICS, SUPPLY CHAINS, AND TECHNOLOGICAL DOMINANCE
summary: Critical minerals have become a central arena of U.S.–China strategic competition because they underpin advanced semiconductors, electric vehicles, renewable energy, aerospace and defense technologies. China’s advantage is not limited to its access to mineral resources; its extensive control over processing, refining, manufacturing, infrastructure and supply-chain networks creates significant vulnerabilities for the United States and its allies. This paper examines how Washington and Beijing are competing to secure critical-mineral supply chains and how efforts to reduce strategic dependence can generate reciprocal threat perceptions and deepen geopolitical rivalry. It examines three strategically important resource regions— the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ukraine, and Greenland—to assess how resource endowments, political instability, infrastructure, foreign investment, and strategic partnerships are shaping the competition. The analysis argues that complete decoupling from China is neither immediately feasible nor strategically desirable. Instead, the United States should pursue supply-chain resilience through domestic mining and refining, strategic stockpiling, recycling and technological innovation, cooperation with trusted allies and deeper engagement with resource-rich states. The paper concludes that critical minerals are increasingly instruments of economic statecraft and geopolitical leverage, and that competition over their supply chains will play an important role in determining the future distribution of technological, economic, and strategic power.

title: Scaling vs. Transforming Climate Finance
summary: This article examines how climate finance can address three longstanding gaps: the lack of integration of science into action, the inequities associated with the adoption of novel technologies, and the lack of voice for individuals with lived experience. Using a comparative qualitative case study of the European Union’s (EU) Green Bond Framework and the South African Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP), this article examines how finance is carried out differently, depending on the circumstances of the developed/developing worlds. The EU example illustrates a high level of scientific integration, in the form of taxonomies, as a mechanism for scaling technology, but exposes the drawback of technocratic isolation. On the other hand, JETP in South Africa demonstrates that finance can be a transformative process that incorporates justice and community involvement, including indigenous knowledge, despite obstacles such as weak governance and structural injustices. Informed by the sustainable development goals (SDGs), the theory of planned behavior, and climate justice principles, this article finds that climate finance needs to focus on both scientific precision and social fairness, as well as on the inclusive scaling of technology and the integration of distributive, procedural, and recognitional justice to act as a transformative vehicle between knowledge and action.

title: An Integrated Indicator-Weight Evolution Method for Sustainable Industrial Supply Chains in Dynamic Scenarios
summary: The resilience and stability of industrial supply chains are the core pillars of the sustainable development of the global economy, and also an important foundation for achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals of “Responsible Consumption and Production” and “Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure”. To address the problem that traditional industrial supply chain risk assessment systems have fixed indicators and static weights, which are difficult to adapt to complex scenarios such as dynamic adjustments of supply chain nodes, fluctuations in market demand and changes in geopolitical patterns, and thus restrict the construction of sustainable supply chain resilience, this paper proposes a comprehensive indicator-weight dynamic evolution algorithm for industrial supply chain risk assessment systems. Firstly, the evolutionary characteristics and trigger rules of the industrial supply chain risk system are defined. Indicator-weight evolution is performed when the original indicator system can no longer meet the evaluation requirements. The Delphi method combined with the actual risk characteristics of the supply chain is adopted to determine the candidate indicator set. The candidate indicators are screened using the grey relational analysis algorithm and the entropy weight-variation coefficient method to construct the evolved risk indicator set. Secondly, an improved DEMATEL model is used to analyze the causal relationships among the evolved indicators. Evolutionary analysis of the original indicator weights is carried out according to the influence degrees between indicators, so as to obtain the evolved indicator weights and realize the dynamic linkage update of evaluation weights. This study conducts a case analysis using publicly available aggregated synthetic data on supply chain disruptions and resilience and compares the proposed method with the entropy weight–analytic hierarchy process (EW-AHP) and dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) methods. The performance of the methods is evaluated in terms of the consistency of indicator weights or relative importance, computational time, out-of-sample prediction performance, and retrospective analysis of a representative disruption event scenario. The results indicate that, under the current case and parameter settings, the proposed method can reconstruct the risk indicator system and coordinate indicator and weight updates, demonstrating certain advantages in computational efficiency and risk factor identification in the specified comparative experiments. It should be noted, however, that the current validation relies primarily on publicly available synthetic aggregated data and retrospective event-scenario analysis. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient to directly establish the risk-warning benefits or improvements in operational response efficiency that the method might deliver in real-world enterprise settings. This study provides a methodological framework for the coordinated updating of indicators and weights in dynamic industrial supply chain risk assessment. Its applicability across industries and practical effectiveness require further validation using independent data sources and actual enterprise operational data.

title: Critical Raw Materials in the Investment Spotlight: Commitments of Foreign Investors and Azerbaijan’s Regulatory Perspective
summary: In recent years, the primary focus of international political debates has been on raw materials essential for economic development.The demand for raw materials critical to the production of modern technological tools, such as cobalt, platinum and lithium, is increasing globally.In general, the processing, development and production of critical raw materials constitute stages of the supply chain and are carried out over a long period, involving enormous investment.For this reason, the intention of foreign investors to make large profits in a short period of time leads to a careless approach to internationally accepted requirements, such as respect for human life, health and the environment.In particular, the dependence of developing countries' economies on these investments leads to a "turning a blind eye" to such violations in those countries and, as a result, to violations of many international obligations assumed by states.Based on the above, the "sustainable" development of the critical raw materials sector is significant for ensuring the well-being of the local population and protecting the environment.This article examines the obligations of foreign investors in this sector and analyzes, in detail, international experience.At the same time, the Critical Raw Materials Act and other European Union documents, which provide the most detailed regulations in this area, are reviewed with respect to their scope of application, the entities they regulate and the obligations they impose on investors and relevant gaps are identified.Additionally, the article examines the availability of critical raw materials in the Republic of Azerbaijan, the regulation of the investment climate in this area and the legal obligations of foreign investors. title: Artificial intelligence promotes urban green innovation in China with regional spillovers and asymmetric climate-risk thresholds
summary: We systematically examine the impact of artificial intelligence on urban green innovation in the context of climate risk. The results demonstrate that artificial intelligence substantially promotes green innovation, an effect primarily transmitted through expanded openness to trade and enhanced scientific-research investment, with the digital economy playing a positive moderating role. Spatial analysis reveals that artificial intelligence advances in one city generate significant positive spillovers that enhance the green innovation performance of neighboring cities. This spatial pattern exhibits pronounced regional heterogeneity: the western region displays significantly positive indirect effects, whereas the eastern and central regions are dominated by direct effects. Threshold effect analysis uncovers differentiated responses to physical climate risks: artificial intelligence’s benefits are weakened once extreme high-temperature days exceed the threshold but strengthened once extreme low-temperature days exceed their threshold, while extreme precipitation exerts no discernible threshold influence. Finally, higher transition risk is found to amplify the beneficial impact of artificial intelligence on green innovation.

title: Do Big4 accounting firms affect foreign individuals’ investment decisions? Evidence from an emerging market
summary: Purpose This paper focuses on an emerging market and investigates whether a firm’s audit engagement with a Big4 accounting firm is associated with foreign individuals’ investments. We hypothesize that Big4 accounting firms’ reputation may function as a heuristic trust signal for these investors. Design/methodology/approach We tested our hypothesis by utilizing 225 non-financial firms listed on Borsa Istanbul. The dataset covers 2005 to 2023 and contains 3,590 firm-year observations. Findings Our empirical evidence indicates that foreign individuals are more likely to invest in BIST-listed firms audited by a Big4 accounting firm (AF). Our results are consistent with prior studies showing that accounting firms’ reputation is associated with investors’ decisions. Our robustness analysis suggests that Big4 AFs’ reputation may lose importance when public governance declines. Research limitations/implications The primary limitation of this research is that investor-level data are not publicly available. We also did not incorporate audit-firm-level variables such as expertise and number of partners. Practical implications Our study has implications for managers, policymakers and accounting professionals. Managers seeking to signal trust to foreign individuals may consider the positive association between Big4 AF engagement and foreign investment. Social implications Policymakers should consider measures to enhance public governance quality to attract more foreign individuals to Borsa Istanbul. Big4 AFs should note that this reputational advantage weakens as public governance declines. Originality/value While prior studies have examined institutional investors’ and mutual funds’ preferences for Big4 accounting firms, this study contributes new archival evidence on foreign individual investors’ equity investment decisions in relation to Big4 engagement in an emerging market context.

title: Green Climate Fund and Eurasian Economic Union: Towards Convergent Interaction of Member States in Climate Finance Area
summary: The purpose of this study was to form and substantiate a theoretical model of coordinated interaction between the EAEU member states and the Green Climate Fund as one of the directions of the Union’s climate agenda. Achieving this purpose was based on the following key methods: 1) the comparative method made it possible to compare the achieved level of cooperation between the member states of the EAEU and the Fund and also the degree of their progress towards direct interaction with latter; 2) the analytical method was used during the consideration of statistical material concerning the negative impact of climate change on the EAEU member states; 3) a systematic approach became the basis for identifying the integration of cooperation with the Fund into the mainstream of the climate agenda of the Union and its member states; 4) the modeling method made it possible to formulate a theoretical structure of possible interaction between the EAEU as an integration association of states and the Fund. The study demonstrated that several EAEU member states (Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Armenia) are actively is carrying out programs and projects supported by the Fund, which not only relate to various sectors, but also support the formation of a mature climate policy in these states. In general, this group of countries is in a stage of transition to a mature institutional phase of interaction with the Fund. The second group of states (Russia and Belarus) do not participate in the Fund’s projects, but maintain specific relations with it. The author substantiates that, despite such divergence, the Union’s climate agenda involves interaction with the Fund at the integration level as some international track for the Union’s positioning. The essence of this track is inclusion in interaction with the global climate finance system.

title: Supply Chain Digital Transformation Misalignment and Supplier Greenwashing: A Dual‐Path Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT Supply chain digital transformation often progresses unevenly across upstream and downstream partners, creating digital transformation misalignment. Drawing on the ability‐motivation‐opportunity (AMO) framework, this study examines how such misalignment affects supplier greenwashing and develops a dual‐path perspective to explain how different directions of digital asymmetry shape supplier responses. Using data on Chinese supply‐chain relationships, we find that supply chain digital transformation misalignment significantly increases supplier greenwashing. Further analyses reveal two distinct behavioural pathways. When suppliers lag behind customers in digital maturity, digital capability constraints limit their ability to undertake and substantiate substantive environmental actions, while relational and transactional pressures increase the incentives to demonstrate environmental responsibility, giving rise to a capability‐constrained symbolic response. In contrast, when suppliers outperform customers in digital maturity, superior information‐processing and information‐control capabilities can weaken customer monitoring and verification, creating opportunities for information‐enabled strategic decoupling. We further identify three mechanisms through which digital transformation misalignment facilitates supplier greenwashing: supply chain information asymmetry, transactional pressure and supervision gaps. In addition, buyer dependency and industry environmental sensitivity amplify the effect of digital transformation misalignment, whereas environmental regulation mitigates it. This study contributes to the supply chain sustainability literature by conceptualizing digital transformation misalignment as a form of sustainability governance imbalance and by demonstrating how different configurations of ability, motivation, and opportunity can generate supplier greenwashing through distinct behavioural pathways. The findings also provide implications for strengthening environmental information governance and monitoring in digitally fragmented supply networks.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE REPORTING AND CORPORATE PERFORMANCE OF LISTED OIL AND GAS COMPANIES IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examined the effect of environmental, social and governance reporting on corporate performance of listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria. The study adopted an ex post facto and correlational research design, using balanced panel data from six listed oil and gas companies: MRS Oil Nigeria Plc, Seplat Energy Plc, Oando Plc, TotalEnergies Marketing Nigeria Plc, Conoil Plc and Eterna Plc. The study period consisted of 60 firm- years (2015-2024). Data were extracted from annual reports, financial statements, sustainability disclosures and corporate governance reports. The components of the ESG reporting were measured using an unweighted disclosure checklist, and corporate performance using the return on assets. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, diagnostic tests and fixed-effects panel regression. The findings showed that environmental reporting had a positive and significant effect on corporate performance, while social and governance reporting had no significant effect. The study concludes that the influence of ESG reporting on performance is not uniform, with the impression that the amount of information disclosed in the environmental section seems more performance- relevant than the social and governance section. It calls for higher reporting quality for the environment, quantifiable reporting results for social initiatives, and meaningful reporting for governance compliance. Keywords: Environmental reporting; social reporting; governance reporting; ESG disclosure; corporate performance; oil and gas companies.

title: ESG Performance and Audit Quality: Bidirectional Relationship and the Moderator Role of Gender Diversity in an International Context
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the bidirectional relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and audit quality and the moderating role of board gender diversity. Using an international sample of 3630 firm‐year observations over 2017–2022, we estimate System GMM and generalized structural equation models. Audit quality is measured using audit fees and audit opinions. The results indicate that ESG performance is negatively associated with audit fees, whereas the reverse relationship is insignificant. This negative association extends to all three ESG pillars. ESG performance is unrelated to audit opinion in the full sample, but the association is positive for low‐ESG firms and negative for high‐ESG firms. By contrast, unmodified audit opinions are negatively associated with ESG performance and with all three ESG pillars. Board gender diversity moderates both directions of the ESG–audit fee relationship, attenuating the negative associations as female representation increases. For audit opinions, moderation occurs only from ESG performance to audit opinion. Overall, the findings reveal substantial heterogeneity across audit‐quality measures, ESG profiles, and board composition.

title: Drilling in ‘paradise’: environmental governance, local communities and oil exploration in the Okavango Delta, Botswana
summary: Abstract Oil exploration in ecologically sensitive landscapes presents significant environmental governance challenges, particularly where extractive development intersects with wetland conservation and community livelihoods. This study examines how international, regional, and national policy and legislative frameworks regulate oil exploration in the Okavango Delta, Botswana, using a qualitative desk-based review of legal, policy, and documentary sources. The findings indicate that Botswana has a comprehensive but fragmented environmental governance framework in which international and regional instruments establish conservation principles and promote transboundary cooperation but depend largely on domestic implementation. National legislation focuses on licensing, environmental impact assessment, and mitigation measures rather than prohibiting exploration in ecologically sensitive areas, while ecosystem-specific policies and wildlife legislation enhance environmental protection through institutional coordination, enforcement, and community participation. The study concludes that the existing governance framework regulates, rather than prevents, petroleum exploration in environmentally sensitive landscapes and recommends strengthening legal safeguards, institutional coordination, and public participation to better balance petroleum development with environmental conservation.

title: Green Transformational Leadership and Green Innovation: The Sequential Mediating Roles of Green Human Capital Management and Work Behavior
summary: Organizations seeking environmental improvement need to understand how leaders' environmental priorities are associated with employee capabilities, everyday conduct, and Green Innovation. This study examined the direct and indirect associations among Green Transformational Leadership, Green Human Capital Management, Work Behavior, and Green Innovation, including a sequential mediation pathway. A cross-sectional quantitative survey of 300 purposively selected company employees used a 24-item, five-point Likert questionnaire; the reported data were analyzed with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. Green Transformational Leadership was positively associated with Green Human Capital Management (β = 0.406; p < 0.001) and Work Behavior (β = 0.255; p < 0.001), but not directly with Green Innovation (β = 0.041; p = 0.446). Green Human Capital Management was associated with Work Behavior (β = 0.325; p < 0.001) and Green Innovation (β = 0.292; p < 0.001), while Work Behavior was associated with Green Innovation (β = 0.326; p < 0.001). The specific indirect paths through Green Human Capital Management (β = 0.118; p < 0.001), through Work Behavior (β = 0.083; p = 0.001), and sequentially through both mediators (β = 0.043; p < 0.001) were significant. These findings support a statistical explanation in which environmental competency management and work conduct connect leadership orientation with perceived Green Innovation, although the cross-sectional design does not establish causal ordering.

title: Research on the Impact and Transformation of Artificial Intelligence Technology on the Development of Traditional Accounting Industry
summary: In the era of digital economy, supported by core technologies such as Robotic Process Automation (RPA), machine learning, and Natural Language Processing (NLP), artificial intelligence has exerted a disruptive impact on the working mode, functional positioning, talent demand and other aspects of the traditional accounting industry. Starting from the application status of artificial intelligence in the accounting field, combined with the core problems existing in the traditional accounting industry, such as low efficiency of manual accounting and delayed information, this paper systematically analyzes the positive impacts and structural changes brought by artificial intelligence through real enterprise cases and other authoritative researches, discusses the challenges in practice, and puts forward targeted coping strategies. It aims to provide a reference for the intelligent transformation of the traditional accounting industry and promote the development of the accounting industry towards a higher-value and more intelligent dimension.

title: Independent in Law, Dependent in Practice: Examining the Effectiveness of Independent Directors Under Indian Corporate Governance Law
summary: India's law requires designated independent directors to satisfy detailed eligibility conditions, disclose conflicts, undertake specified duties and sit on committees that supervise financial reporting and appointments. The assumption behind these rules is that a director who lacks disqualifying ties will be able to judge management proposals without undue influence. That assumption is incomplete. A person may comply with every statutory condition yet depend on promoters or an incumbent board for nomination, access to information, committee assignments and a second term. This article examines that dependence through the Companies Act, 2013, the SEBI listing regulations, regulatory reform papers and selected disputes. It argues that the appointment process deserves closer scrutiny than the usual catalogue of independence tests. The law now offers important counterweights, including special-resolution approval and a limited alternative involving public-shareholder support; neither makes the process wholly independent of concentrated ownership. Satyam and IL&FS show what oversight systems are asked to do when management information is unreliable, but do not prove that every independent director in those companies was culpable. A comparison with the United Kingdom and United States suggests reforms centred on nominations, independent information channels, dissent records and evidence-based accountability. The proposed standard measures independence by the director's freedom to question, investigate and, when necessary, oppose the people who secured the appointment.

title: From Digital Transactions to Formal Credit: A Review of FinTech-Enabled MSME Financing in India – The Role of Alternative Data, Account Aggregators and Digital Public Infrastructure
summary: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a crucial role in India's economic development by contributing to employment generation, entrepreneurship, innovation and inclusive economic growth. Despite their significant contribution, limited access to formal and affordable credit remains a major challenge for MSMEs, particularly small and emerging enterprises. Traditional credit assessment mechanisms largely depend on collateral, financial statements and established credit histories, often restricting the financing opportunities of enterprises operating in the informal and semi-formal sectors. In this context, the rapid evolution of Financial Technology (FinTech), digital payment systems and Digital Public Infrastructure has created new opportunities to transform the MSME financing ecosystem. The present study aims to review existing literature on the role of FinTech-enabled financial services in improving formal credit accessibility among MSMEs in India. It specifically examines the potential contribution of digital transaction records, alternative data-based credit assessment, Account Aggregator frameworks, digital lending platforms and Artificial Intelligence-based credit scoring mechanisms in facilitating access to institutional finance. The study further explores how digital financial information can reduce information asymmetry, enhance creditworthiness assessment and improve the efficiency of lending decisions. Based on a thematic review of twenty selected research studies and academic contributions, the paper identifies emerging opportunities, challenges and developments in technology-driven MSME financing. Particular attention is given to issues relating to data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, digital infrastructure and financial exclusion. The review highlights that although FinTech innovations have the potential to improve credit accessibility, their effectiveness depends on digital adoption, data quality, enterprise formalisation, lender practices and appropriate regulatory safeguards. The study identifies significant research gaps in integrating digital payment data, alternative credit assessment mechanisms and actual formal credit outcomes within the Indian MSME context. It proposes a conceptual framework for understanding the relationship between digital financial infrastructure, data-driven credit assessment and MSME financing outcomes. The paper contributes to the existing literature by highlighting the importance of responsible, transparent and inclusive FinTech-based financing mechanisms for strengthening the financial sustainability and growth of MSMEs in India..

title: DETECTION OF EARNINGS MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THROUGH DISCRETIONARY LOAN LOSS PROVISIONS AT RURAL BANKS IN WEST JAVA, CENTRAL JAVA, AND EAST JAVA DURING THE SAK EP TRANSITION PERIOD (2023–2025)
summary: This study examines whether the transition from the rule-based PPAP provisioning regime to the judgment-based CKPN regime under the Indonesian Financial Accounting Standards for Private Entities (SAK EP) is accompanied by a change in the intensity of earnings management through discretionary loan loss provisions (DLLP) in rural banks (Bank Perekonomian Rakyat/BPR). The novelty of the study lies in using 2023–2025 as a transition window that combines the last two years of the PPAP regime and the first year of the CKPN regime in a single sample, allowing the link between the scope of accounting discretion and income smoothing to be observed among small, unlisted banks, a segment rarely examined in the bank earnings management literature. Panel data of 556 conventional BPRs (1,649 bank-year observations) in West Java, Central Java, and East Java are analysed using a two-stage estimation approach. The results show that non-performing loans are an important determinant of loan loss provisions, whereas pre-managed earnings are positively associated with DLLP, consistent with income smoothing. This association is weak under the PPAP regime but becomes markedly stronger in the first year of CKPN adoption, accompanied by a higher share of banks showing strong discretion, mostly in the form of over-provisioning. The findings enrich positive accounting theory by suggesting that the intensity of income smoothing is not constant but is associated with the scope of judgment permitted by accounting standards, and they offer implications for risk-based supervision by OJK and LPS during the early implementation of SAK EP.

title: From Managerial Ability to Climate Action: The Mediating Role of Corporate Governance in Achieving SDG 13 in the UK Context
summary: ABSTRACT In line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (UNSDG) 13, which emphasizes the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change, this study investigates the role of managerial ability and corporate governance in shaping firms' climate change commitments. Using a sample of 4056 firm‐year observations from companies listed on the London Stock Exchange over the period 2013–2022, the analysis employs ordinary least squares regression, complemented by generalized method of moments and two‐stage least squares estimations to address potential endogeneity concerns. Drawing on stakeholder theory and upper‐echelons and Institutional theory, the findings reveal that greater managerial ability is positively associated with more substantial corporate commitments to addressing climate change, reflecting managers' enhanced oversight capacity, strategic orientation, and ethical awareness. Moreover, the results indicate that corporate governance mechanisms partially mediate the relationship between managerial ability and climate change commitment, underscoring their role in translating managerial competencies into practical climate actions. This study contributes to the environmental and corporate governance literature by providing empirical evidence on the importance of organizational ability and governance structures in advancing corporate climate strategies and supporting the achievement of the climate objectives outlined in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

title: Evolution Patterns, Structural Characteristics, and Convergence Types of Digital Economy Industry Convergence
summary: The convergence of digital and traditional industries is a critical pathway for advancing modern industrial systems in digital economy era. This study employs input-output data from China to measure the degree of industry convergence from both the supply and demand sides. Through clustering analysis and network modeling, the research reveals heterogeneous convergence patterns, primarily characterized by growth and stability, and a trend toward concentration in core clusters dominated by digital and service industries, especially on the demand side. Among digital sub-industries, Digital factor-driven industry demonstrates the most substantial influence, contributing significantly to bidirectional convergence. Digital product service and Digital product manufacturing play key roles on the demand side, while Digital technology application industry shows relatively limited impact. Furthermore, this study identifies varying convergence types across industries, underscoring the need for differentiated, industry-specific policy approaches. These findings provide empirical insights into the structure and dynamics of industry convergence and offer strategic guidance for promoting the deep convergence of digital and traditional economies.

title: Pengaruh CEO Characteristic terhadap Earnings Management pada Perusahaan Subsektor Ritel yang Terdaftar dalam Bursa Efek Indonesia Tahun 2021-2025
summary: Karakteristik Chief Executive Officer (CEO) merupakan salah satu faktor yang dapat memengaruhi pengambilan keputusan dan kebijakan perusahaan, termasuk dalam praktik manajemen laba. Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh usia CEO, jenis kelamin CEO, dan pendidikan CEO terhadap Manajemen laba pada perusahaan subsektor ritel yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2021–2025. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder berupa laporan keuangan tahunan. Sampel penelitian terdiri dari 19 perusahaan dengan 95 observasi yang dipilih menggunakan metode purposive sampling. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan regresi data panel dengan bantuan EViews 12. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa usia CEO berpengaruh negatif tetapi tidak signifikan terhadap manajemen laba. Sementara itu, jenis kelamin CEO dan pendidikan CEO berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap manajemen laba. Secara simultan, usia CEO, jenis kelamin CEO, dan pendidikan CEO berpengaruh signifikan terhadap manajemen laba. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa karakteristik CEO, khususnya jenis kelamin dan pendidikan, berperan dalam menekan praktik manajemen laba, sedangkan usia CEO bukan merupakan faktor utama yang menentukan praktik tersebut. Temuan ini memberikan implikasi bahwa karakteristik pimpinan perlu menjadi pertimbangan dalam memahami kualitas pelaporan keuangan dan praktik manajemen laba pada perusahaan subsektor ritel.

title: Digital Finance for Agriculture: Mobile Money, FinTech, Credit Access and Smallholder Investment
summary: Digital finance promises to lower the costs of financial transactions, expand rural savings and credit, and improve the timing of agricultural investment. Yet access to an account is not equivalent to access to suitable finance, and the movement from digital transactions to farm productivity is neither automatic nor uniform. This critical narrative review examines peer-reviewed evidence on mobile money, digital savings, algorithmic credit, payment digitisation, and their relationships with smallholder investment, risk management and livelihoods. Evidence from randomised trials, panel studies, observational farm surveys, qualitative research and recent reviews is compared with attention to causal identification, agricultural seasonality, inclusion and consumer protection. The strongest findings concern reduced transfer frictions and improved opportunities for remittance-based consumption smoothing. More conditional evidence links mobile payments and savings to specific productive inputs; incentives and the timing of liquidity often determine whether financial access changes investment. Recent experimental work on agricultural digital credit shows greater input spending without reliably demonstrated improvements in harvest output or profits. Consumer risks, including data misuse, opaque pricing and adverse credit reporting, complicate welfare assessments. The review argues that agricultural digital finance should be appraised as an interconnected system of payments, liquidity, insurance, market relationships and safeguards rather than as an isolated application or financial inclusion metric. Research priorities include seasonally timed randomised evaluations, long-term farm profitability, distributional effects, interoperable value-chain payments and transparent risk-adjusted consumer outcomes. Digital finance may relax consequential frictions, but durable agricultural benefits depend on product design, institutions and the broader production environment.

title: Can policy-induced fair competition promote firm cooperative green innovation? Evidence from China’s Competition Review System
summary: Amid the global pursuit of sustainable development, aligning competition policy with green innovation has become an important institutional challenge. This study examines the impact of China’s Fair Competition Review System (FCRS) on firms’ cooperative green innovation (CGI), using a quasi-natural experiment based on panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2023, excluding the 2016 transition year. The results show that firms in regions with greater pre-policy market segmentation experience larger post-FCRS increases in CGI, whereas independent green innovation does not change significantly. The increase is evident in both firm-firm and firm-university/research-institute co-patenting. The effect is stronger in regions with higher marketization, areas where the FCRS is embedded in government performance assessment, and among high-tech and state-owned enterprises. Channel tests are consistent with improved green innovation disclosure, stronger market competition, and lower transaction-related cost burdens. Further analysis shows that the FCRS reduces inefficient investment, increases environmental investment and narrows green total factor productivity gaps. Its effect is also strengthened by low-carbon city policies, environmental taxation and green credit policies. These findings highlight the role of fair competition policy in supporting cooperative green innovation and green transformation.

title: Digital transformation and marketing synergy in the sustainable development of tourism enterprise
summary: In the modern era, the rapid and continuous development of digital technologies has had a significant and multidimensional impact on the management systems, marketing strategies, and customer relationship management of enterprises operating in the tourism sector. The concept of digital transformation is not limited to the implementation of new technological solutions; it also requires the reconfiguration of organizational culture, employee behavior patterns, internal and external communication mechanisms, and social interactions in accordance with the modern digital environment. This process necessitates the adoption of more flexible management approaches in tourism enterprises and creates conditions for improving both internal efficiency and customer-oriented service quality. The main purpose of this study is to comprehensively examine the interrelationships between organizational behavior, social interaction, and marketing synergy in tourism enterprises, as well as to determine the impact of these factors on overall marketing performance. The article analyzes, from theoretical and conceptual perspectives, the influence of organizational behavior patterns and social interactions on marketing outcomes in the context of digital transformation. The research findings indicate that enhancing employee motivation, improving leadership quality, establishing effective internal and external communication systems, and integrating digital marketing tools within a unified strategy play a crucial role in strengthening the competitiveness and market position of tourism enterprises. Furthermore, the interaction of these factors enables organizations to increase customer satisfaction, ensure service personalization, and create longterm loyalty.

title: How do green market orientation, green innovation and leadership styles interact for green new venture creation among family-owned enterprises?
summary: Purpose Drawing on stakeholder theory and leader-member exchange theory, the study examines how a firm's tactical green market orientation – the implementation of eco-friendly marketing tactics – influences green innovation and, in turn, results in successful green new venture creation under different leadership styles. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from family-owned micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) involved in green initiatives in Oman using snowball sampling and analyzed to test the proposed model using partial least squares structural equation modeling in Smart PLS version 4.1.1.8. Findings The findings revealed that tactical green market orientation positively influences green innovation, and green innovation positively influences green new venture creation. Green innovation significantly mediates the relationship between tactical green market orientation and green new venture creation. Finally, the study found a positive but insignificant moderating impact of leadership styles on the associations of tactical green market orientation, green innovation and green new venture creation. Originality/value The results highlight the crucial interplay among tactical green market orientation, green innovation and hybrid leadership styles in promoting sustainable new venture creation in the unique context of family-owned MSMEs. The study offers theoretical and practical implications for family business stakeholders and policymakers in Oman, emphasizing the role of family-owned MSMEs in advancing sustainable industrial innovation and responsible business practices aligned with the SDGs. This investigation aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 9 and 12) by highlighting how sustainable green marking practices and green innovation in small businesses contribute to a resilient industry and responsible production.

title: Renewable energy consumption, financial assistance, and eco-economic sustainability in developing countries
summary: Sustainability remains a major challenge for developing economies, where efforts to promote economic growth must be balanced with environmental protection. This study examines the impact of renewable energy consumption on economic and environmental sustainability in developing countries and investigates whether financial support strengthens these effects. Using panel data for 107 developing countries over the period 2000–2023, the study evaluates the relationships among renewable energy consumption, economic growth, and CO₂ emissions. It examines the moderating roles of foreign direct investment (FDI) and green finance. The findings indicate that renewable energy consumption significantly reduces CO₂ emissions, thereby contributing to environmental sustainability, but is associated with a negative effect on economic growth. Further, financial support significantly moderates the relationship between renewable energy consumption and sustainability outcomes. In particular, FDI and green finance strengthen the emissions-reducing effect of renewable energy while also amplifying its negative association with economic growth. These findings highlight the importance of designing financial and policy frameworks that facilitate renewable energy transitions while addressing their potential short-term economic costs. The study contributes to the sustainability literature by demonstrating that the effectiveness of renewable energy consumption depends not only on its direct environmental benefits but also on the financial conditions under which the transition occurs in developing economies.
