title: Blockchain-driven transformation in supply chain management: A decade of lessons, gaps, and strategic pathways for business leaders
summary: This paper examines how blockchain technology addresses persistent supply chain challenges, fragmented operations, weak traceability, and low stakeholder trust, while identifying strategic pathways for business leaders. A systematic literature review was performed on peer-reviewed documents indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect from January 2016 through December 2025. Following PRISMA-guided screening and quality appraisal, the final analytical corpus comprised 53 high-impact studies, supplemented by sector-specific case analyses in agriculture, healthcare, and manufacturing. The findings reveal that blockchain enables real-time data sharing, reduces fraud through immutable record-keeping, and automates compliance via smart contracts, with consortium blockchains (e.g. Hyperledger Fabric) demonstrating effectiveness in agri-food traceability, achieving up to 18% spoilage reduction. However, implementation barriers persist public blockchains process fewer than 100 transactions per second versus centralized systems exceeding 10,000 TPS; interoperability between permissioned and permissionless networks remains unresolved, and fewer than 5% of studies provide empirical validation of return on investment. For policymakers, we recommend adaptive governance frameworks that balance data privacy (GDPR compliance) with cross-jurisdictional standardization. For industry executives, the study provides actionable pathways including hybrid blockchain architectures that integrate with existing IoT and AI infrastructure, energy-efficient consensus protocols (Proof-of-Stake, PBFT) that circumvent the sustainability paradox of Proof-of-Work systems, and stakeholder-specific adoption roadmaps. The paper’s primary contribution is a decade-spanning synthesis that moves beyond theoretical propositions to deliver empirically grounded, sector-contingent strategic guidance, positioning blockchain not as a technological panacea but as a deliberately deployable instrument for supply chain resilience in a digitally connected economy.

title: Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat: Edukasi Strategi Kemitraan dan Jaringan Bisnis
summary: Digital technology advances and intensifying competition are changing the business environment, requiring business actors to improve adaptability and collaboration. Partnerships and business networks can expand market access, optimize resources, and support business sustainability. This Community Service (PkM) activity aimed to strengthen participants’ understanding of partnership strategies and business networking for business development. It was conducted online through Zoom on August 27, 2026, in collaboration with the Association for Research in Management, Entrepreneurship, and Business Sciences (ARIMBI). Participants included academics, practitioners, entrepreneurs, and students. Activities comprised presentations, interactive discussions, and question-and-answer sessions. The materials covered identifying potential partners, building trust, communicating collaboratively, and using digital technology to broaden business networks. Participants learned about selecting partners whose goals and capabilities match business needs, maintaining mutually beneficial relationships, and sustaining cooperation through effective communication. Digital platforms were discussed as tools for connecting with potential partners and accessing broader business opportunities. The activity is expected to improve participants’ knowledge and readiness to establish productive partnerships, strengthen competitiveness, use resources effectively, and promote sustainable business growth in a changing market within an increasingly digital economy.

title: INTERNAL LOGIC AND NEW DEVELOPMENT ADVANTAGES OF NEW-QUALITY PRODUCTIVE FORCES FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF TOTAL FACTOR PRODUCTIVITY
summary: As essentially advanced productive forces, new-quality productive forces take substantial improvement of total factor productivity (TFP) as its core symbol, which is an inevitable choice for China’s modernization drive. Against the background of new-growth-driver transformation, this paper interprets the theoretical connotation of TFP, analyzes the internal logic that new-quality productive forces realize growth-driver transformation relying on TFP from the perspective of demographic constraints. The Solow residual method is adopted to measure China’s TFP from 2001 to 2025, followed by international comparison. The results show that China’s TFP presents phased fluctuation: it maintained high growth after China’s accession to WTO, turned stable after the global financial crisis, and suffered short-term shocks during the pandemic. There is still considerable catching-up space for China’s TFP compared with developed economies such as the United States. At present, the marginal benefit of economic growth driven by traditional factors is gradually decreasing, and efficiency improvement has become a key path to break through growth bottlenecks. A unified national market, complete industrial system, real-economy-oriented digital economy and booming green low-carbon economy constitute four major advantages for China to improve TFP and foster new-quality productive forces. It provides practical support for quality-oriented economic growth and theoretical reference for central regions to develop new-quality productive forces according to local conditions.

title: Developing an AI Driven Human Resource Development Framework for Sustainable Tourism Villages
summary: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the tourism industry, requiring tourism villages to strengthen their human resource capabilities in order to remain competitive while preserving local cultural values. This study aims to develop a comprehensive Human Resource Development (HRD) framework that supports the digital transformation of Indonesian tourism villages in the AI era. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed by combining quantitative and qualitative approaches. Quantitative data were collected through structured questionnaires administered to 215 tourism village workers across Java and Bali, while qualitative data were obtained from 15 semi-structured interviews with village leaders and three Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) involving tourism stakeholders. The findings reveal substantial gaps in digital competence and AI readiness, with only 18% of respondents reporting prior exposure to AI technologies and 82% demonstrating low-to-moderate digital literacy. Qualitative analysis further identified concerns regarding workforce displacement, the importance of community-based learning, and the need for locally contextualized training programs. Based on these findings, this study proposes a four-pillar HRD framework consisting of digital literacy and AI awareness, contextualized training programs, collaborative learning models, and continuous monitoring and evaluation. The proposed framework provides a culturally responsive and scalable strategy to enhance workforce adaptability, foster sustainable tourism development, and strengthen the resilience of Indonesian tourism villages in the era of AI-driven transformation.

title: Digitalization of tax administrations in European Union: a multi-criteria analysis of digital performance and cross-country disparities
summary: This study assesses the level of digitalization of tax administrations in the 27 Member States of the European Union, applying the PROMETHEE II outranking method to 16 evaluation criteria. Denmark and the Netherlands rank highest. The leading performers share a common profile: they have integrated advanced digital technologies, strengthened their technological infrastructure and developed integrated digital services, drawing on artificial intelligence, process automation, cloud computing, blockchain and interoperable information systems. The analysis also reveals marked differences among Member States, reflecting a complex mix of economic, institutional and technological conditions, including the availability of financial resources, government stability, the maturity of digital culture and the current state of information systems. The GAIA analysis identifies Robotic Process Automation (RPA) as the criterion most closely aligned with the overall ranking, while artificial intelligence and virtual assistants contribute positively, though more weakly, to the differentiation among tax administrations. Overall, the results confirm PROMETHEE II as a reliable tool for monitoring comparative digital maturity and as a useful decision-support framework for a coherent and sustainable digital transformation of tax administrations across the European Union.

title: Developing graduate employability through a credit-bearing, curriculum-embedded internship: an education–industry partnership case from Japan
summary: Purpose To examine how a credit-bearing, curriculum-embedded graduate internship in Japan develops graduate employability and how reflection translates specialised academic knowledge into professional judgement. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative case study of a year-long graduate course at a university in Japan in which postgraduate students worked with industry and public-sector partners on digital transformation challenges. Questionnaires were completed by 16 students, seven instructors and four partner organisations, combining Likert items and open-ended responses; these were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by descriptive statistics used to contextualise the qualitative findings. Findings Students reported gains in career relevance, problem-solving and cross-disciplinary communication. Four themes emerged: authentic data work strengthened analytical capability; reflection translated specialised knowledge into professional judgement; interdisciplinary collaboration fostered boundary-crossing communication; and tensions between innovation and feasibility, autonomy and scaffolding, and academic and partner expectations became productive sites of learning. Research limitations/implications The study examines a single programme at one university using self-report data, so findings are analytically rather than statistically generalisable; comparative and longitudinal research is needed. Practical implications The case identifies four transferable design principles for graduate work-integrated learning and education–industry partnerships: curricular embedding, structured reflection, scoped authentic ambiguity and explicit interdisciplinary facilitation. Originality/value A rare empirical account of a year-long, curriculum-embedded graduate internship in Japan, reframing graduate employability as the development of professional judgement through structured reflection rather than the accumulation of discrete skills.

title: Decomposing the Short and Long‐Run Effects of ESG Performance and Materiality on Corporate External Financing Needs
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) performance on corporate external financing needs (EFN), using a global panel comprising 3437 firms and 11,075 firm‐year observations. Drawing on theories from institutional, risk management and behavioral finance, we decompose short‐ and long‐run dynamics using correlated random effects models, addressing endogeneity through two‐stage least squares (2SLS) estimations. Our findings show that higher ESG performance significantly reduces EFN, with the greatest benefits accruing over the long term. Formal mediation analysis reveals that this relationship operates through four economic channels: enhanced asset tangibility, improved free cash flow generation, eased financial constraints and superior investment efficiency. A key contribution of this study is the identification of a U‐shaped relationship between the materiality of ESG reporting and EFN. Above an optimal threshold, information overload and compliance costs dominate, thereby increasing EFN. We also document that the mitigating effect of ESG varies across pillars and time horizons. These results emphasize the temporal, contingent and mechanism‐driven nature of ESG in corporate financing, providing actionable guidance for managers and policymakers seeking to align sustainability practices with financial resilience.

title: Influência da acreditação hospitalar no uso do orçamento
summary: This study aimed to examine, from the perspective of institutional theory, how hospital accreditation influences budget use in a philanthropic hospital. A descriptive, qualitative single-case study was conducted, with data collected through interviews and questionnaires involving a clinical manager and an administrative manager, as well as a review of the institution’s accreditation manual. The unit of analysis was a philanthropic hospital with level 1 accreditation from the Organização Nacional de Acreditação (ONA). The results showed that hospital accreditation, which certifies the quality and safety of healthcare services, did not influence the introduction of budgeting, as this tool had already been incorporated into the organization following a change in corporate governance. However, accreditation contributed to the continued use of the budget and to adjustments in its planning and execution framework to meet quality and safety requirements. From the perspective of Institutional Theory, evidence of all three forms of institutional isomorphism and of different levels of budget institutionalization was identified. The budget was also found to be used instrumentally, as an integral part of the hospital’s planning, control, and resource allocation routines.

title: Business Process Reengineering Evolution and Business Model Integration Using a Systematic Review
summary: This study systematically examines the evolution of Business Process Reengineering (BPR) research and its integration with business model innovation from 2015 to 2025. It aims to analyze how BPR supports organizational transformation, strengthens digital capabilities, and creates value through business model operationalization. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted on 197 peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus using the keywords “business process reengineering”, “business process”, “reengineering” and “business model”. The review followed the PRISMA framework, while Biblioshiny and VOSviewer were employed for bibliometric analysis and visualization. The findings reveal four stages in the evolution of BPR research. The first stage (2015–2017) emphasized information technology integration and project management to improve process efficiency. The second stage (2018–2020) focused on technology-driven applications, including the Internet of Things (IoT) and supply chain optimization. The third stage (2021–2022) highlighted blockchain, digital twins, and sector-specific innovations in public services and banking. The latest stage (2023–2025) is characterized by AI and machine learning-enabled BPR, supporting intelligent process redesign and customer-centric transformation within the Industry 4.0 context. This study contributes by systematically linking BPR evolution with business model operationalization frameworks, including SDBMOM, ARPM, and the Compass Method, demonstrating how process transformation drives strategic value creation. The findings also show BPR’s contribution to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 8, 9, and 12 through enhanced productivity, innovation, and sustainable production. Future research should examine long-term organizational impacts and cross-sector implementation of AI-enabled BPR.

title: Enhancing port operational performance through flexibility and organizational transformation: the mediating role of digital adoption
summary: The rapid development of digital technologies has profoundly impacted port operations, driving digital transformation to maintain competitive advantage and operational resilience. However, the role of organizational capabilities such as flexibility and transformation in facilitating digital adoption and improving port operational performance remains underexplored. This study proposes and tests a structural model that examines how organizational flexibility and transformation influence digital adoption and port operational performance, with digital adoption serving as a mediator. This study is grounded in Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Technology-Organization-Environment Framework, and the Resource-Based View. The study employed PLS-SEM to analyze the data. The sample consisted of managerial respondents representing 103 container ports in Indonesia, with each response treated as a port-level observation. The results show that flexibility and organizational transformation positively influence digital adoption, but digital adoption does not significantly enhance port performance. The findings suggest that organizational flexibility positively and significantly influences digital adoption, whereas organizational transformation does not have a significant direct effect on digital adoption. Digital adoption positively and significantly enhances port operational performance. Furthermore, digital adoption significantly mediates the effects of organizational flexibility and organizational transformation on port operational performance. These findings highlight the importance of organizational flexibility and the effective adoption of digital technologies as key mechanisms for achieving measurable performance improvements in port operations.

title: Assessing hybrid efficiency through data envelopment analysis: the role of board diversity in Italian benefit corporations
summary: Purpose This study examines efficiency and governance characteristics in Italian Benefit Corporations, the first European adoption of the American Benefit Corporation model. These hybrid enterprises combine the pursuit of profit with legally protected common-benefit objectives embedded in their bylaws. The analysis explores how board composition influences firms' capacity to transform resources into value added with a dual purpose, contributing to profitability while generating resources for common-benefit objectives. Design/methodology/approach Using data envelopment analysis and truncated regression on a sample of 230 firms, the study measures efficiency and assesses whether board gender, age, and nationality affect performance outcomes. Findings The results indicate moderate to high economic-financial efficiency. Gender diversity is positively associated with efficiency, board age heterogeneity is negatively associated with efficiency, and nationality diversity shows no significant influence. Originality/value By integrating efficiency assessment with governance determinants, the study extends data envelopment analysis research to Benefit Corporations and connects the efficiency and corporate governance literature. The findings highlight that different dimensions of board diversity are associated with organisational efficiency in different ways, offering implications for the governance of hybrid organisations.

title: Public Utility Governance Under Scrutiny: An Independent Documentary and Legal Analysis of SIA "Ķekavas nami" (2023–2026)
summary: Abstract This independent documentary and legal study examines the governance, financial accountability, regulatory compliance, and transparency of SIA “Ķekavas nami”, a municipally owned public utility company in Latvia, during the period 2023–2026. Drawing on publicly available financial statements, independent auditor reports, corporate governance documents, tariff information, and municipal shareholder decisions, the study identifies significant questions requiring further examination. The analysis addresses: Financial performance, including the substantial decline in reported profit between 2024 and 2025. The relationship between operating costs, personnel expenditure, management remuneration, and regulated utility tariffs. The increase in wastewater treatment costs and the transparency of tariff calculations. Accounting and asset revaluation issues highlighted in the independent auditor's report. The financial and governance implications of the 2025 corporate reorganisation involving SIA “BŪKS”. Municipal shareholder oversight, corporate accountability, and the accessibility of supporting financial documentation. The distinction between financial statement auditing, regulatory tariff supervision, and the verification of individual residential property management charges. Legal Framework The study considers relevant Latvian legislation governing municipal capital companies, financial reporting, public utility regulation, water services, residential property management, and access to information. Key Conclusion The available documentation establishes a basis for targeted independent scrutiny of accounting practices, cost allocation, tariff transparency, corporate governance, and municipal oversight. However, the identified discrepancies and risk indicators must not be treated as proof of fraud, unlawful tariffs, or misconduct without further examination of primary accounting records, contractual documentation, regulatory decisions, and other relevant evidence. Research Status Independent documentary and legal analysis. This publication is not a statutory financial audit, judicial determination, or official finding of regulatory misconduct. title: IMPLEMENTAÇÃO DE UM PORTAL ACADÊMICO PARA O INSTITUTO SUPERIOR POLITÉCNICO LUSÍADA DO HUAMBO
summary: The digital transformation of higher education institutions has increased the need for solutions that facilitate access to institutional and academic information. This study aimed to develop an academic portal for Instituto Superior Politécnico Lusíada do Huambo in order to organize and provide academic and institutional information in a centralized and accessible environment. The study was characterized as applied and descriptive research, using direct observation, semi-structured interviews and questionnaires to identify users' needs and system requirements. The study involved 11 participants, including five students, three lecturers and three administrative staff members. Based on the information collected, functional and non-functional requirements were identified and used to guide the development of the solution. The portal was developed using WordPress, supported by graphic editing tools, and structured to provide institutional information, academic programmes, departments, administrative staff and other relevant content. The results demonstrate the development of a web-based solution aligned with the initially identified requirements. Further systematic tests of functionality, performance, security and usability should be conducted and reported to strengthen the evaluation of the proposed solution.

title: Urban Measures against Digital Exclusion: Findings from German (Smart) City Strategies
summary: This study investigates measures that cities take to address the digital divide. It examines the extent to which cities’ strategy documents contain measures designed to ensure digital participation and prevent exclusion. The research is based on a survey of digitalization and Smart City strategy documents from 55 medium-sized German cities. A multi-stage methodological approach was applied, combining automated text extraction, systematic key-word searches, and qualitative content analysis for inductive category development. Our analysis reveals widespread rhetorical commitment to digital inclusion, but significant variation in the specificity of measures. An imbalance between symbolic objectives and actionable strategies is observed. A typology of six measure types was developed. The distribution of these measure types shows that most cities prioritize implementation-level actions, particularly communication-oriented instruments. Structural and institutional measures are mentioned far less frequently. Our research provides an analytical model that differentiates between strategic vs. operational and normative vs. concrete approaches to address the digital divide. It offers policymakers and researchers a systematic tool for evaluating and developing inclusive digital transformation strategies in an era of rapid digital developments in the fields of AI and the CitiVerse, which, despite their potential, are also capable of deepening the digital divide.

title: The impact of teamwork on the competitiveness of human capital in IT companies
summary: The article examines how teamwork affects the competitiveness of human capital in IT companies amid digital transformation and Ukraine’s post-war economic recovery. The study aims to support theoretical approaches and practical recommendations for increasing teamwork competitiveness through human capital development and collaborative synergy. The methodological framework is based on systemic and interdisciplinary approaches, as well as theoretical generalization, analysis and synthesis, comparison, structural-functional analysis, systematization and classification, causal and SWOT analysis. The study identifies the organizational, innovative, digital, and communicative components that determine IT teams’ competitiveness. The study substantiates the principles of effective teamwork, including flexibility, cross-functionality, digital interaction, continuous learning, knowledge sharing, innovation, and adaptability to technological changes. The study develops a structural-functional model of IT firm innovation performance that integrates company resources, team formation mechanisms, human capital development, and innovation outcomes. The model considers team formation as a strategic mechanism for transforming individual competencies into collective human capital through trust, psychological safety, communication, knowledge sharing, Agile practices, and digital HR technologies. The study demonstrates that strengthening human capital and team interaction contributes to productivity, innovation activity, employee adaptability, talent retention, and the competitiveness of IT companies. Practical significance lies in applying the findings to team-building programs, corporate learning, digital HR transformation, knowledge-management platforms, and strategies for the post-war development of Ukraine’s IT sector. title: Разработка стратегии управления персоналом предприятия молочной промышленности
summary: Цель работы — разработка научно обоснованной стратегии управления персоналом предприятия молочной промышленности, основанной на анализе лучших мировых практик и адаптированной к современным условиям цифровой трансформации. title: Benchmarking the Business Model of Bank Syariah Indonesia Against International Best Practices: A Comparative Literature Review
summary: The development of Islamic banking in Indonesia still faces challenges in Sharia governance, product diversification, risk management, digitalization, and regulatory harmonization when compared with practices in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and Malaysia. This study aims to analyze these gaps and to identify strategies for strengthening the competitiveness of Indonesian Islamic banking. It applies a PRISMA-based comparative literature review and a bibliometric analysis of 20 academic sources published between 2008 and 2026, with the discussion covering ten strategic dimensions of Islamic banking. The review identifies several main challenges: the dominance of murabahah financing, Sharia governance and supervision that are not yet optimally standardized, limited integration of financial technology, regulatory fragmentation, and the insufficient incorporation of sustainability indicators and Maqasid al-Shariah into performance measurement. It also draws attention to benchmark practices, namely centralized Sharia supervision, a more consolidated legal framework, product diversification, and the adoption of financial technology. The study concludes that improving the competitiveness of Indonesian Islamic banking calls for stronger governance, the development of profit-sharing-based products, regulatory harmonization, and digital transformation. Its contribution lies in a multidimensional comparative synthesis that serves as a conceptual basis for developing a hybrid performance index, one that integrates financial, digital, and sustainability aspects grounded in Sharia principles. These findings can serve as input for regulators and Islamic bank managers in formulating policies and strategies for sustainable industry development.

title: Key audit matters and audit report lag in the Saudi governance context: Does auditor type matter?
summary: This study examines the relationship between key audit matters (KAM) disclosures and audit report lag (ARL) in the Saudi capital market and investigates whether this relationship is moderated by auditor type. Using feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) on a panel dataset of 832 firm-year observations for firms listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) over the period 2016–2021, the study finds that the number of KAM is positively associated with ARL, consistent with recent studies (Bajary et al., 2025; Cameran & Campa, 2025), suggesting that a greater number of KAM reflects increased audit complexity and audit effort, thereby requiring additional time to complete the audit. The results also show that this relationship is significantly stronger for firms audited by Big 4 auditors (Deloitte, PricewaterhouseCoopers [PwC], Ernst & Young [EY], or KPMG), and insignificant for those audited by non-Big 4 auditors. The findings remain robust across alternative model specifications and variable measurements. The study extends the audit reporting literature by demonstrating that the effect of KAM disclosures on audit report timeliness depends on auditor type. The findings also provide practical implications for regulators, investors, and auditors by highlighting that greater audit transparency through KAM may require additional reporting time and audit effort, particularly for Big 4 auditors.

title: Adapting Knowledge and Human Resources to Digital Entrepreneurship in Tourism
summary: The digital transformation of tourism and hospitality businesses has been studied mainly as a matter of business models, platforms, and technology adoption, while the cognitive and organizational-learning processes that determine whether the workforce adapts at the pace of technological change have received less attention, especially in the small and micro enterprises that dominate the sector. Following a theory-synthesis approach, this conceptual paper integrates three frameworks, each selected because it explains a different level of the adaptation problem: (a) the SECI model of tacit-to-explicit knowledge conversion (organizational knowledge flow); (b) the Metacognitive Creative Destruction (MCD) model, which explains how individuals deliberately abandon outdated mental schemas before constructing new ones (individual and group cognition); and (c) research on AI sycophancy, the documented tendency of large language models trained with human feedback to agree with users rather than challenge them (technological context). Their integration leads to a claim that none of the three makes separately: AI use intensity and the density of contradiction that employees actually encounter are distinct variables, and the relationship between them depends on how AI tools are configured and how managers design work. The framework is developed into ten research propositions, each stating a single directional relationship, together with a measurement logic for empirical testing. The paper sets out a research agenda and concludes that, in tourism businesses whose service depends on tacit, experiential knowledge, staff are a central source of competitive advantage and that using this knowledge requires sustainable, employee-centred human resource management.

title: Research on the Financing Status, Dilemmas, and Optimization Paths of Low-Altitude Economy Enterprises under the Digital Economy
summary: As a vital carrier of new quality productive forces and a nationally strategic emerging industry, the low-altitude economy is entering a critical window of scale-up development; however, its financial supply system significantly lags behind the pace of industrial expansion. Against the backdrop of deep integration between the digital economy and the low-altitude economy, this paper adopts a mixed-methods approach combining literature review, policy text analysis, and semi-structured interviews to systematically examine the financing status of low-altitude economy enterprises, analyze their dilemmas and underlying causes, and propose optimization paths. The study finds that the financing of low-altitude economy enterprises exhibits a structural feature of “debt-financing dominance, insufficient direct financing, and high policy dependence.” The mismatch between asset-light structures and collateral logic, the absence of rights confirmation, valuation, and disposal mechanisms for data assets, and the dual uncertainty of policy and technology jointly constitute the core causes of financing constraints, while the financing pain points of the three enterprise types—R&D-oriented, operation-oriented, and infrastructure-oriented—show significant heterogeneity. The digital economy can build a tiered and classified financing model, open the transformation channel of “data resources—data assets—data capital,” and, supported by risk-sharing and digital risk-control mechanisms, systematically reduce financing costs and information asymmetry. This paper provides a reference for low-altitude economy enterprises to broaden financing channels and for relevant stakeholders to optimize decision-making.

title: Perceived competitiveness as an antecedent of strategic governance: adaptive signals in Ibero-American MSMEs
summary: Purpose This study analyzes whether current perceptions of business competitiveness are associated with the future strategic orientation of organizational governance in Ibero-American MSMEs, with an emphasis on Honduras. Unlike traditional approaches, this work inverts the analytical logic and examines perceived competitive signals (environment and internal performance) as antecedents of future corporate governance decisions. Design/methodology/approach The research adopts a quantitative and explanatory-comparative approach, with data from the survey of the 2024 Ibero-American MSME Report by FAEDPYME (7,762 companies in 12 countries) (FAEDPYME 2024). The Perceived Business Competitiveness Index (PBCI), with environment and performance dimensions, and the Strategic Governance Perspective Index (SGPI), derived through (k-means) and distances to centroids, are constructed. The association is evaluated with OLS models with country fixed effects and robustness analysis with fractional models. Findings The perception of internal performance is positively and statistically significantly associated with the future strategic orientation of governance, while the perception of the competitive environment does not present a significant association once business characteristics and country heterogeneity are controlled for. This pattern suggests that the future governance orientation (towards continuity, professionalization or succession) responds more to confidence in perceived internal capabilities than to the reading of external conditions. The Honduran subsample maintains the same direction for the performance component, although with lower statistical significance, while the environment component is also not significant in the Honduran case. Practical implications The findings have differentiated implications for two audiences. For MSME managers, they suggest that governance decisions (continuity, professionalization and succession) are more linked to confidence in perceived internal performance than to the reading of the external environment, which invites strengthening internal capabilities as a basis for anticipatory strategic planning. For public policymakers and business support institutions, the results support the design of differentiated interventions according to the company's strategic profile, with special attention to MSMEs facing greater restrictions in internal capabilities. Originality/value The study inverts the traditional logic by positioning perceived competitiveness as an antecedent and not as a result of the future strategic orientation of governance, opening an adaptive reading of the phenomenon. As a methodological contribution, it proposes the SGPI as a continuous indicator constructed through unsupervised learning.

title: Designing and Validating an AI Accountability and Auditability Framework for Financial Reporting: Lessons from Enron, WorldCom, and SOX Logic (AI-SOX-FR)
summary: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into financial reporting introduces profound accountability and auditability challenges, echoing historical corporate scandals like Enron and WorldCom. This working paper introduces the AI Accountability and Auditability Framework for Financial Reporting (AI-SOX-FR), a comprehensive 5-layer architectural model (Data Lineage, Model Governance, Explainability, Audit Receipts, and Shadow Auditing) designed to bridge the gap between advanced machine learning systems and traditional Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance logic. By synthesizing historical control failures with modern algorithmic risks, this research provides a rigorous pathway for listed companies to ensure transparent, verifiable, and GAAP-compliant automated reporting.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Food Supply Chains: Distribution Optimization and Waste Reduction
summary: One-third of the food made for people to eat gets. Thrown away but the tools used to fight this issue mostly only look at how well we can predict it (Onyeaka et al. 2025). This chapter says that just predicting won't cut down on loss. Waste happens at points where decisions are made. How much to restock when to send out goods how to divide up products when to lower prices and how to get rid of things. These points aren’t fixed just by better predictions. The chapter connects three ways of looking at the problem with the real-life ways that fresh food ends up being thrown guessing how much people will want figuring out how long food will last based on basic chemistry and temperature effects and planning how to deliver food in a way that deals with it being perishable time limits and pollution. The proof includes a 14.8% drop in food waste per store and 26,705 tonnes of CO₂ not released because of AI in stores (Onyeaka et al. 2025) predicting how long food will last with changing storage conditions (Rashvand et al., 2025) using AI to watch and support recycling efforts (Onyeaka et al. 2023) and a look at 104 studies about food loss before it gets to people between 2015 and 2024 (Ma et al. 2026) that showed prevention isn’t getting much attention as fixing things later. Three main points are made: that knowing what is happening matching loss with solutions keeping limits and making sure everyone has the right reasons to help together set limits on what AI can do; that expanding the cold chain is only worth it if the extra energy needed is less than the waste it stops; and that when people say something is good, for the environment they need to say exactly what they mean show how sure they are and tell where the waste is really going.

title: From orchestrated resources to supply chain performance: the indirect role of power
summary: Purpose The study applied resource orchestration and resource dependency theories to examine how firm resources affect supply chain performance in Ghana's food and beverage industry, as well as the mediating role of power. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach and explanatory design were employed using survey data collected from firms in Ghana's food and beverage sector. Out of the 427 questionnaires distributed, 395 usable responses were obtained. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling to assess direct and specific indirect effects. Findings The results indicate that human, financial and innovation resources significantly enhance supply chain performance, whereas relational and structural resources do not exert direct effects. Power positively influences performance and serves as a critical mechanism, with both partial and full mediation observed across resource categories. The findings reveal that resource value is heterogeneous and context-dependent, and that performance gains are realised when resources are effectively translated into influence that aligns with partner behaviour. Originality/value The study advances the literature by moving beyond the composite view of firm resources and demonstrating that resource effects are not uniform but context-specific. It further positions power as a central mechanism linking resource deployment to performance, offering a more context-sensitive explanation of supply chain dynamics in developing economies.

title: Adaptive and Distributed Leadership for Digital Transformation: Building Resilient and Connected School Systems
summary: Digital transformation challenges school leaders to maintain continuity, respond to technological change, and coordinate collective action. Objective: This study explored how adaptive and distributed leadership were practiced by school leaders, how these practices were perceived to strengthen resilient and connected school systems, and the challenges and opportunities encountered. Methods: A qualitative descriptive design was used with eight school leaders from the Caloocan North II District, Schools Division of Caloocan City, during school year 2025–2026. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using the thematic approach identified in the source dissertation as Boyatzis’ approach. Results: The analysis organized participants’ accounts into three overarching themes: (1) adaptive and distributed leadership as foundations for collaborative digital transformation; (2) shared leadership practices as foundations of school resilience and connectedness; and (3) challenges and opportunities in applying these leadership approaches during digital transformation. Described practices included responsiveness to teacher readiness, revising digital plans, piloting tools, delegation, communication, and peer coaching. Reported constraints included resistance to change, unreliable connectivity, limited devices, and uneven digital competence. Conclusion: Participants described adaptability and shared responsibility as useful strategies for coordinating digital initiatives and sustaining school operations amid disruption. A seven-area leadership development program was proposed; its effectiveness was not evaluated in this study.

title: The Power of Behavioral Antecedents in Predicting Supply Chain Performance of Crop Seed Enterprises
summary: This study examined whether opportunistic behavior, supply chain collaboration, social bonds (supply chain socialization) and human resource practices predict supply chain performance, measured as quality, response time, productivity and financial/cost performance, in crop seed enterprises in Kenya. Guided by social exchange and systems theories, a quantitative survey was conducted of 143 crop seed enterprises registered in Kenya as of 2024. Data were collected from supply chain heads, operations officers or their equivalents in public and private seed companies and analyzed using structural equation modeling, with each driver tested in a separate prediction model. Each hypothesis was partially supported, with one performance dimension significantly related to each driver. Opportunistic behavior significantly lowered quality (b = ?0.40, p = .036). Supply chain collaboration (b = 0.225, p = .040) and human resource practices (b = 0.225, p = .033) were positively associated with productivity, while social bonds were associated with shorter response times (b = ?1.024, p = .034). No driver significantly predicted financial/cost performance at the .05 level. Crop seed enterprises should curb opportunism through clear contracts and quality verification, invest in collaboration and human resource practices to raise productivity, and build partner socialization to improve speed, with support from seed associations like Seed Trade Association of Kenya (STAK) and regulators like Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS). The study contributes to behavioral prediction models of multidimensional supply chain performance in an under-researched agricultural input sector. title: DEEP LEARNING BASED DETECTION OF ANOMALOUS INVENTORY FLUCTUATIONS IN INDUSTRIAL SUPPLY CHAINS
summary: Fluctuations in inventories across industrial supply chains are caused by interplay between demand, ordering, replenishment, and production which makes it challenging to detect anomalies with just one threshold or simple distributional rules. In this paper we introduce an anomaly detection approach based on four synchronized time series (inventory, demand, ordering, and replenishment). Our model captures normal operating patterns through sliding windows and computes the difference between actual and estimated inventory level as an anomaly score. We tested our model over a 240-step simulated sequence including sudden inventory drops and persistent inventory surpluses; for this sequence the multivariate model obtained an F1 score of 0.897 and an AUC of 0.951, surpassing Isolation Forest, LSTM, GRU, and baseline Transformer models. Detected anomalies matched the injected anomaly events. Results indicate potential use of multivariate time-series modeling for inventory anomaly screening, however, further validation is needed on real-world enterprise data.

title: The Influence of Corporate Governance on Firm Performance: Intellectual Capital as A Mediating Variable in Listed Mining Companies (2021-2024)
summary: Purpose: This study examines the relationship between Corporate Governance (CG) and Firm Performance (FP) and investigates the mediating role of Intellectual Capital (IC). Focusing on mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2024, the study explores whether intellectual capital helps explain the relationship between governance mechanisms and firm performance in a capital-intensive industry. Design/methodology/approach: This quantitative study uses purposive sampling to select 22 mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, yielding 88 firm-year observations for 2021–2024. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with WarpPLS 8.0. Corporate Governance is represented by ownership structure and board characteristics. Intellectual Capital is assessed through Human Capital Efficiency (HCE), Structural Capital Efficiency (SCE), and Relational Capital Efficiency (RCE). Firm Performance is measured using Return on Assets (ROA), Return on Equity (ROE), and Net Profit Margin (NPM). Findings: The results show that CG has a positive and statistically significant relationship with FP (β = 0.185, p = 0.035). However, CG has a negative and statistically significant relationship with IC (β = −0.260, p = 0.005), contrary to the hypothesized positive direction. IC has a positive but statistically insignificant relationship with FP (β = 0.051, p = 0.316). Furthermore, the indirect effect of CG on FP through IC is negative and statistically insignificant (β = −0.013, p = 0.431). Thus, the results do not provide sufficient statistical evidence to support IC's proposed mediating role. The model assessment also indicates limited explanatory power, suggesting that other factors may contribute to variation in mining companies’ financial performance. Practical implications: Mining companies should strengthen governance practices while evaluating how they develop and use intellectual capital. Managers should not assume that investments in human, structural, and relational resources automatically produce immediate financial gains. Instead, they should assess how these resources are integrated into organizational processes and business strategies. Industry stakeholders may also consider initiatives that build knowledge and strengthen organizational capabilities. Originality/value: This study contributes sector-specific evidence on the relationship among CG, IC, and FP in an emerging market. Its findings highlight the negative association between CG and IC and the lack of statistically significant evidence for the proposed indirect effect. The study also emphasizes the importance of considering additional explanatory factors when examining governance and financial performance in the mining sector.

title: Slimming the fossil mammoth: financing defossilisation, from supply chains to end uses (Fossil Carbon Notebooks, Notebook 9)
summary: Slimming the fossil mammoth: financing defossilisation, from supply chains to end uses. Fossil Carbon Notebooks, Notebook 9. Working version 0.9 This notebook quantifies, item by item, what defossilising the economy requires, and shows how to finance it within the Geological Net Zero Pact. The pact aims to return to the subsurface, step by step, as much fossil carbon as is extracted. Producers and sellers of fossil carbon would be responsible for the carbon they extract and place on the market, including what they consume themselves. The notebook starts from 36.15 GtCO₂ of fossil emissions in 2024 (EDGAR) and divides them into five intervention families: distributed generation; transport; peaking plants; internal operations of the fossil fuel industries; power, heat and industry. For each item, a simple model separates the emissions that can be avoided from those that can be captured on the remaining flows. Across three scenarios, avoidance ranges from 8.9 to 20.8 GtCO₂ a year and the capture potential from 11.5 to 14.2 Gt. The central “balanced combination” scenario avoids 14.3 Gt and captures 14.2 Gt. The engine of the system: every tonne avoided at the customer’s site is carbon not extracted, for which the producer is no longer answerable and which it does not have to return to the subsurface. Within an appropriate framework, producers will therefore have an interest in co-financing any adaptation that avoids a tonne for less than the cost of a return, around $60–150 per tonne on the first capture and storage chains. The pact leads to three business models, aligned with the three carbon accounts of the founding article: Common infrastructure. A geological atlas, the characterisation of sequestration units and shared networks, financed by the Pact Fund: 110-115 billion dollars a year for an indicative levy of 3$/tCO₂ . The fossil obligation. It rises on a fixed timetable and is met by geological return or by co-financing customers’ energy transition. Removals. Durable storage of biogenic and atmospheric CO₂ in the same infrastructure, under separate accounting. Scaling up is the main challenge. Capture and storage capacity in operation today is 50–64 MtCO₂ a year, more than two hundred times below the central capture potential. The atlas and the characterisation of storage sites must therefore be financed early. Contents of this record: full and condensed versions, in French and English. The document sets out a proposal and orders of magnitude, with no deployment timetable; it does not constitute investment advice. title: Assurance and ESG rating divergence can limit the informational value of sustainability disclosure mandates
summary: Abstract Regulators increasingly treat disclosure quantity as the principal policy lever, assuming that more sustainability disclosure yields better-informed investors and more efficient capital allocation. This conceptual paper argues that the assumption is misspecified. Disclosure moves investor beliefs only insofar as it is credible, and credibility is manufactured downstream of the reporting entity, by assurance providers who verify and rating agencies who aggregate. We develop the construct of the credibility wedge, the gap between the quantity of sustainability information a firm discloses and the reliability investors attach to it. Drawing on costly state verification, cheap-talk and signalling models, ambiguity-based asset pricing and institutional theory, we specify a three-layer architecture of preparer, assurer and rater, each with a distinct failure mode. Twelve propositions connect regime design to the wedge, and the wedge to belief revision, the cost of capital and capital allocation. A two-by-two typology is derived and applied to the four architectures observable in 2026: the narrowed European regime, jurisdictions adopting IFRS S1 and S2, the United States, and India’s BRSR Core. As the wedge grows, the marginal informational return to additional disclosure tends to zero, implying that verification and rating infrastructure must be built before disclosure scope is widened. India offers an unusually favourable research setting, and eight estimable models are specified. For the 2030 Agenda, target 12.6 and its report-counting indicator track disclosure volume rather than decision-useful information, making credible verification a precondition for reporting to advance SDGs 12 and 13.

title: Human Capital Reporting in the Era of ESG: Analyzing HRA Disclosures and Transparency in Leading FMCG Companies in India
summary: In the current business environment global ESG frameworks and traditional financial reporting have intertwined to redefine the organization value paradigm. The Human Capital Development(HCD) and Human Resource Accounting(HRA) have evolved from secondary disclosures to primary markers of a sustainable corporate strategy. Against the global context of sustainability ever so much at the forefront of corporate behaviour, and the impending imposition of mandatory regulatory rationale to ESG standards (e.g., the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR)that SEBI has heard will come into force), this paper investigates human capital reporting and disclosures in five leading Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) companies in India (Hindustan Unilever, Dabur India, ITC, Britannia, and Nestle) as pioneers of practices that seek to achieve improved accountability in the coverage of significant parameters of the Subject Core Component. This study synthesizes recent literature across both emerging and developed markets to propose an integrated theoretical model of how ESG-driven HRA disclosures are associated with organizational governance and corporate performance. This paper used a content analysis study of top Indian FMCG companies including Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), ITC Limited, Dabur India and Nestle India to examine disclosure behaviour, reveal structural reporting gaps, and evaluate the influence of attributes of companies on human resource disclosure index. The preliminary finding is that tier-one Indian FMCG companies perform well on international ESG metrics on training, diversity, and occupational health, although the actual measuring of HRA metrics is not common and is usually not standardized in large-mid-sized firms. Finally, this study provide a framework for investor engagement to improve human capital transparency in EMs, alongside actionable policy recommendations.

title: Journeying through Digital Transformation: Experiences of Teachers and Administrators in the Adaption of Digital Professional Development in Public Schools
summary: This study examined teachers’ and school administrators’ experiences of Digital Professional Development (DPD) in selected rural public schools in Bohol, Philippines. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was used, in which survey responses from 348 educators—305 teachers and 43 school administrators—preceded the analysis of 19 written accounts from 13 teachers and six school administrators. A 100-item, four-point questionnaire measured engagement, challenges, and coping and adaptation. Responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics and nonparametric tests (Mann–Whitney U, Kruskal–Wallis H, chi-square, and Spearman correlation), while the written accounts were examined through thematic analysis. Overall engagement was high (M = 3.19), with very high perceived relevance (M = 3.35) and participation rated lowest among the dimensions (M = 3.07). Challenges were also high (M = 3.06), led by workload and time demands (M = 3.16) and technological and access barriers (M = 3.11), and coping and adaptation were high (M = 3.23). Overall engagement differed by role, age group, and educational attainment and was associated with service and DPD-attendance categories, while gender differences were not significant (p = .504). Engagement was positively related to challenges (rₛ = .205) and to coping and adaptation (rₛ = .629), both p < .001. Six themes emerged: useful learning in everyday work; infrastructure, time, and confidence gaps; collegial help, practice, and resourcefulness; uneven institutional support; practical, sustained, and equitable DPD; and gradual progress and adaptation. Recognized usefulness thus coexisted with continuing barriers to participation and application. The integrated evidence supports practical training, protected learning time, reliable resources, and continuing peer and institutional assistance, which informed a proposed six-month action plan built around a six-hour practical training activity. Because the evidence is self-reported and integration was conducted at the group level, the findings establish neither causal effects nor improvements in learner outcomes.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Financial Reporting Quality in the Nigerian Public Sector
summary: This study examined the effect of AI-enabled financial management systems, proxied by Government Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS) adoption, on financial reporting quality in the Nigerian public sector. Specifically, the study assessed the effect of GIFMIS adoption on the timeliness and completeness of financial reporting among federal Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs). The study adopted a quantitative longitudinal panel research design using secondary data obtained from the annual financial reports of selected federal MDAs for the period 2014–2024. A purposive sample of 50 federal MDAs, yielding 550 MDA-year observations, was analyzed using panel regression techniques. Fixed Effects and Random Effects estimators were considered, while the Hausman specification test was used to select the appropriate model. Institutional size and budget size were included as control variables, with standard errors clustered at the MDA level. The findings revealed thatGIFMIS adoption had a statistically significant negative effect on reporting lag (β = −18.42, p < 0.01), indicating that adoption was associated with an average reduction of approximately 18.42 days in the time required to prepare and release financial reports. GIFMIS adoption also had a statistically significant positive effect on the completeness of financial reports (β = 0.142, p < 0.01), suggesting improved inclusion of required financial statement components and disclosures. The study concludes that technology-enabled financial management through GIFMIS can enhance important dimensions of financial reporting quality in the Nigerian public sector. It recommends sustained GIFMIS implementation, improved system integration, continuous technical support, and standardized reporting procedures across federal MDAs.

title: Neuro-Fuzzy System Dynamics for Effective Risk Management in Off-Site Construction Supply Chains
summary: Abstract This research presents a novel neuro-fuzzy system dynamics (NN-Fuzzy-SD) model designed to manage risks in off-site construction supply chains (OCSCs). By combining the predictive power of neural networks (NNs) with the uncertainty-handling capabilities of fuzzy logic, the model enables dynamic, real-time risk assessment and mitigation, addressing challenges such as material shortages, transportation delays, and labor disruptions. The model integrates real-time data to optimize inventory buffers, resource allocation, and scheduling strategies, improving project efficiency and resilience. An empirical case study across six off-site construction projects in Beijing and Shanghai demonstrates the model’s effectiveness in adapting mitigation strategies according to varying risk profiles, yielding measurable improvements in cost efficiency and operational performance. This study makes four primary contributions to construction engineering and management. First, it introduces the first integrated NN-Fuzzy-SD framework for real-time risk management in off-site construction. Second, it develops the dynamic risk mitigation strategy optimization (DRMSO) and cross-domain neuro-fuzzy decision support system (C-DNF-DSS) for adaptive, cross-domain mitigation. Third, it empirically validates the model with real-world projects, providing quantitative evidence of improved resource allocation. Finally, it identifies dominant risk drivers and delivers a scalable, industry-ready framework that enhances project resilience, operational efficiency, and informed decision-making, contributing significantly to the global construction management body of knowledge.

title: Diagnosing Barrier Interrelationships in International Modular Construction Supply Chains: A Hierarchical Grey DEMATEL Framework
summary: Abstract International modular construction can improve quality, schedule performance, and labor efficiency, but its supply chains are exposed to cross-border barriers that remain insufficiently understood as an integrated construction-management problem. Existing barrier studies are useful for identifying salient constraints, yet they provide limited insight into how barriers interact and propagate across international modular delivery systems. This study investigates these interrelationships in international modular construction supply chains using a hierarchical grey decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory (G-DEMATEL) framework. Based on literature review, contextual analysis, and expert consultation, 26 barriers were identified and organized into four categories. The framework integrates grey linguistic assessments to capture uncertainty in expert judgments, objective expert-weighting schemes based on certainty and consensus, and hierarchical reconstruction of the global interaction matrix to reduce elicitation burden while preserving systemic interdependence. The results show that supply chain, production reliability, and skills barriers constitute the most prominent category, whereas international regulatory and financial barriers exhibit the strongest causal role. At the global level, Incoterms and risk-transfer ambiguity, shipment-classification ambiguity, and uncertain customs-clearance time emerged as the most prominent barriers, while fragmented regulations and jurisdiction across countries acted as the strongest upstream causal driver. These findings indicate that visible operational disruptions are often downstream effects of upstream regulatory, commercial, and governance uncertainty. The study contributes by explaining barrier propagation in international modular delivery as a cross-border engineering-management system and by providing a scalable decision-support approach for prioritizing earlier interventions related to contracting clarity, customs readiness, coordination, and logistics planning.

title: Pricing and Coordination of a Dual-Channel Supply Chain Considering Price Reference Effect and Return Service
summary: With the development of dual-channel supply chains, consumers have more purchasing options, and reference price effects have become increasingly important in shaping their purchasing decisions. To attract consumers, some suppliers and retailers need to adjust their pricing strategies and provide measures such as return services to gain more profits. To address these problems, considering that the reference price effect and return service level are important factors affecting the supply chain, we construct game-theoretic models for a manufacturer-dominated dual-channel supply chain comprising one manufacturer and one retailer, use them to examine the optimal decisions, and analyze the effects of the reference price effect and return service level on the supply chain. Then, a two-part pricing contract is developed. The results show that, within the feasible parameter region, a higher return service level improves the total supply chain profit. In the parameter regions examined, a stronger reference price effect increases the manufacturer’s online channel demand and revenue, whereas the retailer’s offline channel demand and revenue tend to decrease when the return service level is relatively low. Furthermore, the manufacturer’s profit increases, while the retailer’s profit may decline at relatively low return service levels. A sufficiently high return service level can mitigate this adverse effect. The proposed two-part pricing contract yields a feasible interval of fixed transfer fees within which the profit conflict between the manufacturer and the retailer can be resolved.

title: Adoption of the Fintech Services among Young Entrepreneurs
summary: The rapid development of financial technology (FinTech) has transformed the delivery and utilisation of financial services, creating new opportunities for entrepreneurs to conduct business transactions, manage finances and access digital financial solutions. Young entrepreneurs represent an important segment of the entrepreneurial ecosystem because of their potential to promote innovation, employment generation and economic development. The adoption of FinTech services can help them improve transaction efficiency, maintain financial records and manage business activities more conveniently. However, the extent of adoption may depend on technological capabilities, financial knowledge, perceived benefits, accessibility, trust and security concerns. Against this background, the present study, titled “Adoption of FinTech Services Among Young Entrepreneurs,” aims to examine the adoption patterns and preferences of FinTech services and analyse the factors influencing their adoption. The study focuses on digital payments, mobile banking, internet banking, digital wallets and online lending platforms. It considers digital literacy, financial literacy, perceived usefulness, ease of use, trust, accessibility and security concerns as potential determinants of FinTech adoption. A descriptive research design is proposed, with primary data collected through a structured questionnaire administered to young entrepreneurs. A sample of 100 respondents may be considered, subject to the availability of participants and the defined scope of the study. Secondary data may be obtained from academic journals, research articles, books and relevant institutional reports. Frequency and percentage analysis, mean scores, standard deviation and correlation analysis may be used to examine the data. Multiple regression may also be employed to identify the relative contribution of selected factors to FinTech adoption. The illustrative analysis presented for this study suggests that digital payments and mobile banking may be widely used by young entrepreneurs, while online lending platforms may have comparatively lower adoption. Perceived usefulness, ease of use and accessibility emerge as important factors to investigate, while trust and security remain relevant considerations. These preliminary, illustrative patterns are not empirical findings and must be verified using actual survey data. The study is expected to provide insights for FinTech service providers, policymakers and entrepreneurship-support organisations in developing accessible, secure and user-friendly financial solutions. It also emphasises the importance of digital and financial literacy in promoting informed and responsible adoption of FinTech services among young entrepreneurs..

title: The Internal Mechanism of Digital Economy Empowering Gansu Province’s Science and Technology Strengthening Action
summary: The Science and Technology Strengthening Action serves as a core strategic starting point for Gansu Province to break the path dependence of resource-based economy, cultivate new quality productive forces, build a modern industrial system, and promote high-quality economic and social development. Compared with developed provinces in eastern China, scientific and technological innovation in Gansu has long been constrained by structural shortcomings including inefficient factor allocation, blocked R&D chains, weak hardware support, insufficient industrial scenarios, and shortage of human resources. The traditional innovation model relying on factor input, experience-driven decision-making and offline collaboration can no longer adapt to the iterative upgrading of scientific and technological innovation in the new era. Characterized by data elements, digital technologies, computing power infrastructure and scenario integration, the digital economy can systematically reshape the paradigm of regional scientific and technological innovation from four dimensions: innovation factor reconstruction, innovation chain reshaping, innovation foundation consolidation and innovation ecosystem iteration, providing a new logic and path for underdeveloped western regions to achieve leapfrog development and quality improvement in scientific and technological innovation. Based on the resource endowments, industrial structure, scientific and technological foundation of Gansu Province and the national strategic location advantages of the Eastern Data, Western Computing initiative, this paper adopts the innovation factor allocation theory, digital innovation theory and new quality productive force theory to systematically deconstruct the deep internal mechanism of the digital economy empowering Gansu’s Science and Technology Strengthening Action. It respectively elaborates the resource reconstruction mechanism of data elements, the full-chain iteration mechanism of digital technologies, the hard-core supporting mechanism of green computing power, and the dynamic activation mechanism of industrial scenarios, and further reveals the coupling and synergistic relationship among the four mechanisms, constructing a four-dimensional empowerment theoretical framework of “factor reconstruction-technology empowerment-infrastructure support-scenario-driven development”. The research shows that the empowerment of the digital economy is not a simple instrumental application, but a systematic, structural and subversive upgrading of regional scientific and technological innovation through factor reform, process reengineering and ecological reshaping, which effectively solves the practical problems of scattered scientific and technological resources, low R&D efficiency, obstructed achievement transformation and insufficient innovation motivation in Gansu. This study enriches the theoretical system of digital science and technology integration in western Chinese provinces, and provides theoretical support and academic basis for Gansu to further deepen the Science and Technology Strengthening Action, promote the in-depth integration of digital economy and scientific and technological innovation, and foster new regional innovation advantages.

title: Digital Transformation of MSMEs in Southwest Nigeria: The Interactive Effects of Infrastructure, Digital Skills, and Policy Environment on Adoption and Firm Performance
summary: Purpose: This study explored the digital transformation of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Southwest Nigeria by investigating the effects of digital infrastructure, digital skills, policy environment, and their interaction on digital adoption and firm performance. The study addressed a gap in the literature by evaluating the possibility of the determinants working independently or in complement to each other in influencing the MSME digital transformation. Methodology: The mixed method research design was used by collecting quantitative data from 240 MSMEs in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo and Ekiti States, while qualitative data was gathered through key informant interviews and focus group discussions. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations and Generalized Linear Models (GLM) were used for analyzing quantitative data, and thematic analysis of NVivo software was used for analyzing qualitative data. Findings: The results show that digital infrastructure is the strongest determinant of digital adoption, followed by digital skills and policy environment. The interaction effects of digital infrastructure and digital skills, digital skills and policy environment, and digital infrastructure and policy environment were statistically significant, showing that these factors are complementary and mutually reinforcing. Furthermore, digital adoption, digital infrastructure, digital skills, and policy environment significantly improve MSME performance. These findings suggest that coordinated investments across all three areas yield greater returns than isolated interventions. The study reveals that digital transformation in MSMES in Southwest Nigeria is attributed to the synergistic effect of digital infrastructure, digital capabilities and policy interventions. Originality: This study contributes to the empirical evidence of the complete interaction between digital infrastructure, digital skills and policy environment in a single econometric specification, showing that all the three factors are complementary and reinforcing as determinants of digital adoption and firm performance among MSMES in Southwest Nigeria. The results broaden the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) approach and provide empirical support for policy recommendations for coordinated policy interventions

title: Digital Transformation in Railway Ticketing: The Role of Passenger Perception and Attitude in Determining Service Satisfaction
summary: Digital transformation has significantly changed the railway reservation system by providing passengers with convenient and accessible online ticketing facilities. In India, the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) and third-party service providers have contributed to the development of digital railway booking services. However, the effectiveness of these platforms depends not only on technological facilities but also on passengers' perceptions, attitudes and satisfaction. This study aims to examine the influence of passenger perception and attitude on satisfaction towards online railway ticketing services, with special reference to Coimbatore City. The study considers important dimensions such as perceived convenience, ease of use, reliability, security, information quality and service responsiveness. A descriptive and analytical research design is proposed, with primary data to be collected through a structured questionnaire from online railway ticket booking users. Percentage analysis, correlation, independent sample t-test and multiple regression are proposed for analysing the data. The study is intended to provide insights into passenger expectations and identify factors that influence satisfaction with digital railway ticketing platforms.

title: When AI takes control, who takes responsibility? Structural analysis of agentic AI risks in supply chains
summary: Purpose Agentic AI systems execute procurement decisions, reroute shipments and renegotiate supplier contracts at speeds that preclude real-time human review. The existing literature offers limited analytical attention to the risks that arise when decision authority is delegated to agents. This paper develops a risk taxonomy for agentic AI in supply chains and traces the hierarchical dependencies and influence magnitudes among the identified risks. Design/methodology/approach A systematic review of literature, analyzed through theories–characteristics–contexts–methods framework, produces the risk taxonomy. A hybrid modified total interpretive structural modeling and fuzzy decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory methodology is then applied to structured expert judgments to establish the causal hierarchy and quantify inter-risk influence. Findings Three risks, namely workforce skill gap, data quality and reliability and ethical misalignment occupy the deepest level of the causal hierarchy. Lack of accountability and governance and data privacy emerge as terminal outcomes. All three analytical methods converge on a conclusion: agentic AI risks originate at the institutional layer, with technical risks acting as transmission mechanisms. Practical implications The findings indicate that effective governance requires that workforce capability, data integrity and objective-function alignment are addressed before deployment. The stratified agentic AI governance framework is proposed that translates hierarchical structure into a sequenced intervention architecture, providing practitioners with governance priorities organized by risk-propagation logic. Originality/value This paper contributes a systematically derived risk taxonomy and a causally weighted governance map for agentic AI risks in supply chains. Five propositions are derived from the causal structure and are advanced as a testable research agenda.

title: Torrefied Agri-Food Residues as a Coal Substitute: How the Supply Chain and the Allocation Rule Determine the Carbon Footprint
summary: Agri-food processing leaves large volumes of lignocellulosic residues for which their energy is rarely recovered, while coal-fired heat and power in Europe carries a rising carbon price. This study quantifies the carbon footprint of five food-processing residues—spent coffee grounds (SCGs), spent tea leaves (TEAs) and walnut, pistachio and peanut shells—with spruce wood chips as a non-food benchmark, torrefied at 250–550 °C and burned in place of Czech lignite. Fuel properties were measured for all six materials at five temperatures and their replicate variances propagated. Emissions were quantified for nine process stages—from cultivation of the crop to combustion of the fuel—per tonne of dry residue under a fuel-first allocation that charges the residue with the agricultural chain and credits the food co-product by system expansion; cut-off, mass and economic allocation were compared. All six materials save emissions at their selected temperature, from −557 ± 22 kg CO2-eq t−1 for SCG to −1214 ± 23 for spruce, avoiding 36–77% of the emissions of the lignite they replace. The ranking is set by the supply chain rather than by the fuel: SCG has the highest calorific value of the set yet saves least, because 89% of its residual burden comes from roasting, brewing and intercontinental freight. The result is conditional: Under mass allocation, four of the five food residues become net emitters, and so do SCG and TEA when collected wet. At 65 EUR tCO2−1, the avoided emissions are worth 36–79 EUR t−1 against a fuel-cost advantage over lignite of 116–200 EUR t−1.

title: Do ESG mutual funds deliver superior performance? Evidence from sustainable investing in the Indian emerging market
summary: The rising trend of sustainable investing and the increasing incorporation of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) criteria into financial decisions have necessitated an assessment of ESG mutual funds’ performance in India. There is limited empirical evidence on whether ESG funds deliver better risk-adjusted returns and the impact of ESG rankings and expense ratios on fund performance. The study employs a quantitative research method to analyze the monthly return data of the ESG mutual funds in India from 2021 to 2025. Risk-adjusted performance measures like the Sharpe, Treynor, Jensen’s alpha and Sortino ratios are used to rank the funds. The funds are compared with the Nifty 50 index and the Fama-French 3-factor model is used to analyze the impact of market, size and value factors on returns. Furthermore, a cross-country Granger Causality test examines the direction of causality between ESG and traditional market indexes in emerging markets. The findings state that the returns of ESG funds are positively correlated with the returns of the benchmark indices and the higher the ESG ranking, the better the fund’s performance, with least effect from expense ratios. The Fama-French analysis indicates that ESG funds did not generate positive abnormal returns over this period. Remarkably, the Granger causality is one-way from ESG to market indices in India, which is attributed to the regulatory framework in the country.
